rows.defer_reason: 'It would be interesting to understand the local limit' is a vague research direction, not a single proposition.

rows.title: Problem 1
rows.paper_title: Spectrally symmetric orientations of graphs
rows.statement_text: Find the minimal constant $\widehat{\rho}\in[0,1]$ such that each spectrally symmetric graph satisfies $\frac{2|E(G)|}{|V(G)|^{2}}\leq\widehat{\rho}$.
rows.context_text: Motivated by the classical fact that a graph of order $n$ with more than $\frac{n^2}{4}$ edges is not bipartite (and hence its adjacency spectrum is not symmetric), the authors ask for an analogous density threshold for spectrally symmetric orientations. The paper establishes $\frac{13}{18}\leq\widehat{\rho}\leq\frac{10}{11}$ but the exact value remains open.
rows.source_text: Find the minimal constant $\widehat{\rho}\in[0,1]$ such that each spectrally symmetric graph satisfies $\frac{2|E(G)|}{|V(G)|^{2}}\leq\widehat{\rho}$.
rows.defer_reason: 'Find the minimal constant' is a determine-the-value problem; known bounds 13/18 <= rho <= 10/11 but no conjectured value.
rows.class_notes: 'Spectrally symmetric' also not precisely defined in this record.

rows.title: Problem 5.1
rows.paper_title: Color-avoiding directed paths in tournaments
rows.statement_text: For some integers $q\geqslant 4$ and $N$, does there exist a non-transitive $q$-edge-colored $N$-vertex tournament whose longest color-avoiding path has strictly fewer than $f_{q,q-1}(N)$ vertices?
rows.context_text: For $q\geqslant 4$, Proposition 1.5 shows $F_{q,q-1}(n)=G_{q,q-1}(n)$, meaning the largest $(q-1)$-comparable set is always a $(q-1)$-increasing sequence and hence corresponds to a transitive tournament. Problem 5.1 asks whether a non-transitive coloring can do strictly worse than the transitive extremum. The answer is affirmative for $q=3$ via the Hamaker–Stein construction, but Proposition 1.5 rules out any vector-based construction for $q\geqslant 4$, leaving the problem open in that range.
rows.source_text: For some integers $q\geqslant 4$ and $N$, does there exist a non-transitive $q$-edge-colored $N$-vertex tournament whose longest color-avoiding path has strictly fewer than $f_{q,q-1}(N)$ vertices?
rows.class_notes: Depends on the paper-local extremal functions f_{q,q-1} and G_{q,q-1}, not defined in this record.

rows.title: Conjecture 6
rows.paper_title: An Induced $A$-Path Theorem
rows.statement_text: For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, every graph $G$ and $X,Y\subseteq V(G)$ satisfies one of the following: $G$ contains $k$ pairwise anti-complete $(X,Y)$-paths; or there exists a set $Z\subseteq V(G)$ with $|Z|\leqslant k-1$ such that $G-N_{G}[Z]$ has no $(X,Y)$-path.
rows.context_text: The authors pose this $(X,Y)$-path strengthening of their main theorem (Theorem 3), seeking to reduce the separator size from $78(k-1)$ to the optimal $k-1$. If true, it would have immediate application to the study of induced minors, in particular implying an Induced Grid Minor Theorem for $K_{1,t}$-induced-subgraph-free graphs conjectured by Dallard et al.
rows.source_text: For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$, every graph $G$ and $X,Y\subseteq V(G)$ satisfies one of the following: $G$ contains $k$ pairwise anti-complete $(X,Y)$-paths; or there exists a set $Z\subseteq V(G)$ with $|Z|\leqslant k-1$ such that $G-N_{G}[Z]$ has no $(X,Y)$-path.
rows.verification_note: Authored in X11.v:induced_menger_anticomplete_paths_statement. Encodes Conjecture 6: every graph and X,Y either has k pairwise vertex-disjoint anticomplete X-Y paths, or a set Z of size at most k-1 whose closed neighbourhood deletion leaves no X-Y path.
rows.class_notes: Induced Menger-type dichotomy with standard vocabulary (anticomplete paths, closed neighborhood); optimal-separator strengthening of the paper's Theorem 3.

rows.title: Problem 1.1
rows.paper_title: Nowhere-zero flow reconfiguration
rows.statement_text: Is it true that for every 2-edge-connected graph $G$, the reconfiguration graph $\mathcal{F}(G,5)$ is connected?
rows.context_text: This is the natural reconfiguration version of Tutte's 5-flow conjecture. The paper notes that Problem 1.1 is incomparable to Tutte's 5-flow conjecture itself, since connectedness of $\mathcal{F}(G,k)$ does not imply non-emptiness. The group-flow analogue is posed separately as Problem 1.3.
rows.source_text: Is it true that for every 2-edge-connected graph $G$, the reconfiguration graph $\mathcal{F}(G,5)$ is connected?
rows.class_notes: The adjacency (reconfiguration step) of F(G,k) is paper-defined and not given in this record.

rows.title: Problem 2.6
rows.paper_title: Nowhere-zero flow reconfiguration
rows.statement_text: Let $G$ be a graph and $k$ be an integer. Prove that if $\mathcal{F}(G,\mathbb{Z}_{k})$ is connected, then $\mathcal{F}(G,k)$ is also connected.
rows.context_text: The paper establishes the easier direction (connectivity of $\mathcal{F}(G,k)$ implies connectivity of $\mathcal{F}(G,\mathbb{Z}_k)$) and provides examples showing the group structure matters. The converse direction is open; the authors note they cannot prove it even for $k=4$.
rows.source_text: Let $G$ be a graph and $k$ be an integer. Prove that if $\mathcal{F}(G,\mathbb{Z}_{k})$ is connected, then $\mathcal{F}(G,k)$ is also connected.
rows.class_notes: Same missing definition of the reconfiguration graphs F(G,k) and F(G,Z_k) as axv_2512_17342_00.

rows.title: Open Question on Circular Drawing Characterisation
rows.paper_title: When all directed cycles have the same weight
rows.statement_text: Is there a theorem that says ``every appropriately connected digraph $G$ contains no thing of type $X$ if and only if $G$ admits a circular drawing''?
rows.context_text: Thomassen's theorem gives a characterisation of circular drawings in the presence of a specific 2-vertex separator. The authors generalise this into a motivating question and, despite fully characterising weightable digraphs in the paper, explicitly state: ``We still have not come up with the characterization we hoped for of the digraphs with circular drawings.''
rows.source_text: Is there a theorem that says ``every appropriately connected digraph $G$ contains no thing of type $X$ if and only if $G$ admits a circular drawing''?
rows.source_locator: arXiv:2601.12746 — Open Question on Circular Drawing Characterisation
rows.defer_reason: Meta-question asking whether some characterization theorem with an unspecified obstruction 'X' exists; no concrete proposition.

rows.title: Problem 1
rows.paper_title: Faster 3-colouring algorithm for graphs of diameter 3
rows.statement_text: Can 3-colouring be solved on diameter-2 graphs in quasi-polynomial time?
rows.context_text: The paper improves the algorithm for 3-colouring diameter-3 graphs, leaving the complexity of 3-colouring diameter-2 graphs as the main outstanding challenge. The authors note this is one of the two 'notorious' open cases identified by Paulusma, and that the polynomial-time solvability of 3-colouring on diameter-2 graphs is the most intriguing open problem in the area. The quasi-polynomial formulation is highlighted as an explicit intermediate target.
rows.source_text: Can 3-colouring be solved on diameter-2 graphs in quasi-polynomial time?
rows.class_notes: Clean yes/no algorithmic question but needs a computation model (quasi-polynomial time).

rows.title: Problem 1
rows.paper_title: Characterization of sparse monotone graph classes with bounded domination-to-2-independence ratio
rows.statement_text: Which graph classes have bounded domination-to-2-independence ratio?
rows.context_text: The domination-to-2-independence ratio of a graph class $\mathcal{G}$ is defined as $\sup_{G\in\mathcal{G}}\tfrac{\gamma(G)}{\alpha_{2}(G)}$. Since the fractional relaxations of domination number and $2$-independence number coincide, a bounded ratio would allow both parameters to be approximated via their common fractional relaxation, computable in polynomial time. The problem has been studied for trees, strongly chordal graphs, dually chordal graphs, outerplanar graphs, and other sparse graph classes.
rows.source_text: Which graph classes have bounded domination-to-2-independence ratio?
rows.defer_reason: 'Which graph classes ...' is an open-ended characterization over all graph classes, not a single proposition.

rows.title: Problem 2
rows.paper_title: Characterization of sparse monotone graph classes with bounded domination-to-2-independence ratio
rows.statement_text: Which graph classes have domination tied to 2-independence?
rows.context_text: A graph class $\mathcal{G}$ has domination tied to 2-independence if there exists a function $h$ such that $\gamma(G)\leq h(\alpha_{2}(G))$ holds for every graph $G\in\mathcal{G}$. This is a relaxation of Problem 1, which requires $h$ to be linear; the authors remark that even this relaxed version seems non-trivial.
rows.source_text: Which graph classes have domination tied to 2-independence?
rows.defer_reason: 'Which graph classes have domination tied to 2-independence?' is an open-ended characterization, not a single proposition.
rows.class_notes: Relaxation of Problem 1 (axv_2601_15082_00) from linear to arbitrary tying function.

rows.title: Problem 4.1
rows.paper_title: Coloring small locally sparse degenerate graphs and related problems
rows.statement_text: What is the maximum fractional chromatic number of a $d$-degenerate, $K_{r}$-free graph?
rows.context_text: Given the main theorem of Martinsson [26] on triangle-free $d$-degenerate graphs and its many applications, the authors seek a generalization of Harris' conjecture for $K_{r}$-free graphs. One might guess the answer is $O_{r}\left(\frac{d\log\log d}{\log d}\right)$ by analogy with Johansson's bound for $K_r$-free graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$, but Theorem 1.6 shows this is not the case.
rows.source_text: What is the maximum fractional chromatic number of a $d$-degenerate, $K_{r}$-free graph?
rows.defer_reason: Determine-the-value / order-of-magnitude question with no conjectured proposition to state.

rows.title: Problem 6.1
rows.paper_title: Coloring small locally sparse degenerate graphs and related problems
rows.statement_text: Can the upper bound $2^{cd}$ on the number of vertices assumed in Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 be weakened to $e^{\omega(d)}$ (with a corresponding improvement of the upper bound on $\chi$ when $n=e^{\omega(d)}$)? What if we additionally assume that the graph has large (constant) girth?
rows.context_text: The perhaps most important open problem left by the paper is whether the exponential requirement on the number of vertices in Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 can be further relaxed. Even improving the constant $c$ in Theorem 1.1 could resolve Erdős's problem on graph Ramsey numbers for all triangle-free graphs by combining with the trivial lower bound $r(G)\geq|V(G)|$.
rows.source_text: Can the upper bound $2^{cd}$ on the number of vertices assumed in Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 be weakened to $e^{\omega(d)}$ (with a corresponding improvement of the upper bound on $\chi$ when $n=e^{\omega(d)}$)? What if we additionally assume that the graph has large (constant) girth?
rows.class_notes: Refers to Theorems 1.1/1.2 not stated in context; also partly meta (improve-the-bound flavor).

rows.title: Problem 6.2
rows.paper_title: Coloring small locally sparse degenerate graphs and related problems
rows.statement_text: Is the following statement true for all $\varepsilon>0$? If $G$ is a $d$-degenerate triangle-free graph with maximum degree $\Delta(G)\leq e^{d^{1-\varepsilon}}$, then we have $\chi(G)=O\left(\frac{d}{\log d}\right)$.
rows.context_text: Resolving this problem would likely require localizing the random coloring process used in the paper so that the union bound can be replaced by an application of the Lovász Local Lemma. An affirmative answer would imply results on immersion analogues of Hadwiger's conjecture, as conjectured by Lescure and Meyniel in 1988.
rows.source_text: Is the following statement true for all $\varepsilon>0$? If $G$ is a $d$-degenerate triangle-free graph with maximum degree $\Delta(G)\leq e^{d^{1-\varepsilon}}$, then we have $\chi(G)=O\left(\frac{d}{\log d}\right)$.
rows.class_notes: Conclusion of the implication is truncated in source; hypothesis side is fully standard.

rows.title: Problem 6.3
rows.paper_title: Coloring small locally sparse degenerate graphs and related problems
rows.statement_text: Is it true that if the chromatic number of a $K_{r}$-free $d$-degenerate graph is $d+1$, then the graph has $e^{\Omega_{r}(d)}$ vertices?
rows.context_text: The main results of the paper establish that triangle-free $d$-degenerate graphs with at most $2^{cd}$ vertices have chromatic number strictly less than $d+1$; this problem asks whether the exponential lower bound on the order of extremal examples extends from the triangle-free case ($r=3$) to all $r$.
rows.source_text: Is it true that if the chromatic number of a $K_{r}$-free $d$-degenerate graph is $d+1$, then the graph has $e^{\Omega_{r}(d)}$ vertices?
rows.class_notes: Self-contained: K_r-free d-degenerate with chi=d+1 forces e^{Omega_r(d)} vertices.

rows.title: Problem 6.4
rows.paper_title: Coloring small locally sparse degenerate graphs and related problems
rows.statement_text: Let $r\geq 4$. Is it true that the maximum fractional chromatic number of $K_{r}$-free $d$-degenerate graphs is $o_{r}(d)$?
rows.context_text: Theorem 1.6 gives a lower bound of $\Omega(d/\log^{(r-2)}d)$ on the fractional chromatic number of $K_r$-free $d$-degenerate graphs, which approaches linear in $d$ as $r$ increases, leaving open whether the maximum is truly sub-linear for each fixed $r\geq 4$.
rows.source_text: Let $r\geq 4$. Is it true that the maximum fractional chromatic number of $K_{r}$-free $d$-degenerate graphs is $o_{r}(d)$?
rows.verification_note: Authored in X218.v:kr_free_degenerate_fractional_chromatic_sublinear_statement. Bradac-Fox-Steiner-Sudakov-Zhang Problem 6.4, stated affirmatively: for r >= 4 and every positive q (standing for epsilon = 1/q) there is d0 such that every d-degenerate graph with omega < r and d >= d0 has fractional chromatic number at most d/q, in X130's attained (a:b)-fold cross-multiplied form x130_frac_chi_le G d q.
rows.class_notes: Bradac-Fox-Steiner-Sudakov-Zhang Problem 6.4: for r >= 4, is the maximum fractional chromatic number of K_r-free d-degenerate graphs o_r(d)? Modelling: chi_f as a rational LP value (b-fold colourings), and o(d) as forall eps=1/q, exists d0, forall d >= d0, q*chi_f <= d.

rows.title: Problem 9
rows.paper_title: Cops and robber in graphs with bounded vertex cover number
rows.statement_text: Is it true that for connected graphs $G$, $\operatorname{cop}(G)=o(\mathrm{td}(G))$?
rows.context_text: The authors ask whether a sublinear bound on the cop number in terms of treedepth holds, viewing treedepth as a natural intermediate parameter between vertex cover number and treewidth. They note that the bound $\operatorname{cop}(G)\leqslant\tfrac{1}{2}(\mathrm{td}(G)+1)$ is easily deducible from existing results on treewidth, but improving significantly on it seems difficult.
rows.source_text: Is it true that for connected graphs $G$, $\operatorname{cop}(G)=o(\mathrm{td}(G))$?
rows.class_notes: Needs cop-number (pursuit game) and treedepth primitives plus little-o wrapper.

rows.title: Conjecture 4.1
rows.paper_title: Long cycles in vertex transitive digraphs
rows.statement_text: There exists an $\varepsilon>0$ and infinitely many values of $n$ for which there exists a connected vertex transitive digraph of order $n$, whose perimeter gap is at least $\varepsilon n$.
rows.context_text: The paper proves the perimeter gap grows at least as fast as $(1-o(1))\ln n$ and that circumference is always at least $\Omega(n^{1/3})$. Determining the best possible bounds seems far out of reach; this conjecture is proposed as a natural intermediate target, asserting that the logarithmic lower bound on the gap is far from tight.
rows.source_text: There exists an $\varepsilon>0$ and infinitely many values of $n$ for which there exists a connected vertex transitive digraph of order $n$, whose perimeter gap is at least $\varepsilon n$.
rows.class_notes: 'Perimeter gap' is paper-local and not defined in the record.

rows.title: Conjecture 4.2
rows.paper_title: Long cycles in vertex transitive digraphs
rows.statement_text: Let $c(n)$ denote the minimum circumference of a connected vertex transitive graph on $n$ vertices. Let $d(n)$ denote the minimum circumference of a connected vertex transitive digraph on $n$ vertices. Then $d(n)=\Theta(c(n))$.
rows.context_text: The paper's bound of $\Omega(n^{1/3})$ on the circumference of connected vertex transitive digraphs is slightly weaker than the best known $\Omega(n^{9/14})$ undirected bound. This conjecture asserts that the directed and undirected cases are asymptotically the same, proposed as a natural intermediate target.
rows.source_text: Let $c(n)$ denote the minimum circumference of a connected vertex transitive graph on $n$ vertices. Let $d(n)$ denote the minimum circumference of a connected vertex transitive digraph on $n$ vertices. Then $d(n)=\Theta(c(n))$.
rows.class_notes: d(n)=Theta(c(n)) fully defined in the statement; circumference and vertex transitivity are standard.

rows.title: Question 4.3
rows.paper_title: Long cycles in vertex transitive digraphs
rows.statement_text: Is it true that in any connected vertex transitive digraph, any two longest directed cycles intersect?
rows.context_text: A major obstacle to translating results from graphs to digraphs is that, unlike 2-connected undirected graphs, strongly 2-connected digraphs may contain vertex-disjoint longest cycles. The authors ask whether vertex transitivity could be a condition guaranteeing intersection of all pairs of longest cycles.
rows.source_text: Is it true that in any connected vertex transitive digraph, any two longest directed cycles intersect?

rows.title: Conjecture 1
rows.paper_title: Packing arithmetic progressions
rows.statement_text: $m(n)\sim\frac{4}{3}\cdot\frac{n^{3/2}}{\ln n}$.
rows.context_text: The paper proves $m(n)=\Theta(n^{3/2}/\ln n)$ with matching constants $4/3$ (lower) and $5/3$ (upper) in Theorem 1. The authors state that closing this gap and pinning down the exact constant requires additional ideas, and suspect $4/3$ is correct.
rows.source_text: $m(n)\sim\frac{4}{3}\cdot\frac{n^{3/2}}{\ln n}$.

rows.title: Conjecture 4
rows.paper_title: Packing arithmetic progressions
rows.statement_text: $M_{\mathbb{P}(n)}(n)\sim\frac{1}{6}\cdot\frac{n^{3}}{\ln n}$.
rows.context_text: Closely related to Conjecture 3. The lower bounds in Conjectures 3 and 4 follow from the proofs of the lower bounds in Theorems 1 and 5, respectively. The upper bounds remain open.

rows.paper_title: Packing arithmetic progressions
rows.statement_text: For every $k$ satisfying $\Omega(\sqrt{n})=k<\sqrt{n}$, we have $m_{k}(n)\sim\left(1-\frac{k^{2}}{3n}\right)\frac{k}{\ln k}\cdot n$.
rows.context_text: If Conjecture 1 holds, it also resolves $m_k(n)$ asymptotically for $k\geqslant\sqrt{n}$ via Theorem 4. The only remaining open case is $k<\sqrt{n}$ with $k\not=o(\sqrt{n})$, which this conjecture addresses.

rows.paper_title: Packing arithmetic progressions

rows.paper_title: Packing arithmetic progressions
rows.statement_text: For every fixed $n$ and $k$ tending to infinity, we have $M_{k}(n)=(1+o(1))nk$.

rows.title: Question 5
rows.paper_title: On Borodin-Kostochka conjecture for correspondence coloring
rows.statement_text: What is the smallest number $\Delta_{0}$ such that every graph $G$ with $\Delta(G)\geq\Delta_{0}$ and $\omega(G)=\Delta(G)-1$ satisfies $\chi(G)=\chi_{\ell}(G)=\chi_{DP}(G)$?
rows.context_text: Theorem 4 of this paper gives an upper bound $\Delta_0 \leq 3\cdot 10^9$ for the correspondence coloring analogue. The equality $\chi(G)=\chi_\ell(G)=\chi_{DP}(G)$ clearly holds for all graphs $G$ with $\omega(G)=\Delta(G)+1$, and the parameters also coincide for graphs with $\omega(G)=\Delta(G)$; the smallest threshold $\Delta_0$ for the case $\omega(G)=\Delta(G)-1$ remains unknown.
rows.source_text: What is the smallest number $\Delta_{0}$ such that every graph $G$ with $\Delta(G)\geq\Delta_{0}$ and $\omega(G)=\Delta(G)-1$ satisfies $\chi(G)=\chi_{\ell}(G)=\chi_{DP}(G)$?
rows.defer_reason: Asks for the exact smallest threshold Delta_0, not a single proposition.
rows.class_notes: DP/list-coloring threshold variant of Borodin-Kostochka (omega=Delta-1 regime), not the conjecture itself.

rows.title: Conjecture 4.1
rows.paper_title: Anticoncentration of random spanning trees in graphs with large minimum degree
rows.statement_text: Let $d$ be sufficiently large, and let $n$ be sufficiently large relative to $d$. Suppose that $G$ is a connected graph with $n$ vertices and minimum degree at least $d$, and let $\mathcal{T}$ be a uniformly random spanning tree of $G$. Then, for every tree $T$ it holds that $$\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{T}\cong T)\leq n^{-(1/2-o_n(1))(d-1)}.$$
rows.context_text: The authors conjecture that the optimal constant factor in the exponent of the anticoncentration bound should be $1/2$, matching the anticoncentration of a uniformly random spanning tree of $K_{d,n-d}$. For $K_{d,n-d}$, a spanning tree up to isomorphism is determined by a minimal subtree connecting the $d$ vertices in the small class and the number of leaves attached to each of these $d$ vertices.
rows.source_text: Let $d$ be sufficiently large, and let $n$ be sufficiently large relative to $d$. Suppose that $G$ is a connected graph with $n$ vertices and minimum degree at least $d$, and let $\mathcal{T}$ be a uniformly random spanning tree of $G$. Then, for every tree $T$ it holds that $$\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{T}\cong T)\leq n^{-(1/2-o_n(1))(d-1)}.$$
rows.class_notes: Uniform random spanning tree anticoncentration; needs probability over finite trees plus o_n(1) exponent.

rows.title: Conjecture 4.2
rows.paper_title: Anticoncentration of random spanning trees in graphs with large minimum degree
rows.statement_text: Let $d$ be sufficiently large, and let $n$ be sufficiently large relative to $d$. Suppose that $G$ is a connected graph with $n$ vertices and minimum degree at least $d$. Then, the number of non-isomorphic spanning trees of $G$ is at least $\Omega(n^{d-1})$.
rows.context_text: The anticoncentration property of Conjecture 4.1 would imply only $n^{(1/2-o_n(1))(d-1)}$ non-isomorphic spanning trees, but $K_{d,n-d}$ has $\Omega(n^{d-1})$ non-isomorphic spanning trees. The authors conjecture that this larger quantity gives an essentially optimal lower bound, with $K_{d,n-d}$ being an extremal example.
rows.source_text: Let $d$ be sufficiently large, and let $n$ be sufficiently large relative to $d$. Suppose that $G$ is a connected graph with $n$ vertices and minimum degree at least $d$. Then, the number of non-isomorphic spanning trees of $G$ is at least $\Omega(n^{d-1})$.
rows.class_notes: Counting non-isomorphic spanning trees; Omega(n^{d-1}) needs asymptotic wrapper.

rows.title: Problem 1
rows.paper_title: A Gray code for arborescences of tournaments
rows.statement_text: Does every graph $G$ admit a pivot Gray code on its spanning trees?
rows.context_text: A pivot Gray code for spanning trees requires that consecutive spanning trees differ by an edge exchange sharing a common endpoint (the strong revolving door property). Although the corresponding reconfiguration graph is connected for any graph $G$, it remains open whether all graphs admit such a code. Pivot Gray codes have been constructed for fan graphs and more generally for outerplanar graphs.
rows.source_text: Does every graph $G$ admit a pivot Gray code on its spanning trees?
rows.class_notes: Pivot Gray code = Hamilton path in spanning-tree exchange graph with common-endpoint pivots; defined in context.

rows.title: Conjecture 6.1
rows.paper_title: Colour-balanced subgraphs
rows.statement_text: Let $h\colon E(K_{n,n})\to\mathbb{R}^{k}$ such that $\|h(e)\|_{1}\leq 1$ for all $e\in E(K_{n,n})$. Then there is a perfect matching $M$ of $K_{n,n}$ satisfying $f_{h}(M)=O(\sqrt{k})$.
rows.context_text: There is a gap between the $O(k^2)$ upper bound for representative matchings in bipartite complete graphs (Section 1.1) and the worst-case lower bound of $\sqrt{k/2}$ constructed in Theorem 5.1. The authors conjecture that the lower bound gives the correct order, so that the true bound is $\Theta(\sqrt{k})$.
rows.source_text: Let $h\colon E(K_{n,n})\to\mathbb{R}^{k}$ such that $\|h(e)\|_{1}\leq 1$ for all $e\in E(K_{n,n})$. Then there is a perfect matching $M$ of $K_{n,n}$ satisfying $f_{h}(M)=O(\sqrt{k})$.
rows.class_notes: Bound O(sqrt k) paraphrased in brackets but content clear: exists C with ||sum_M h(e)||_1 <= C sqrt(k).

rows.paper_title: Colour-balanced subgraphs
rows.statement_text: There exists some absolute constant $C$ such that for all positive integers $k$ and $t$, every colour-balanced $k$-edge-colouring of $K_{2kt}$ admits a perfect matching $M$ satisfying $f_{c}(M)<C$.
rows.context_text: There is a gap between the $O(k^2)$ upper bound from Theorem 1.2 and the constant lower bound constructed in Theorem 5.3 for matchings in complete graphs. The authors conjecture the constant lower bound is tight. They note that a $\sqrt{k}$ lower bound for perfect matchings of $K_{kt,kt}$ implies that new ideas would be necessary to prove this conjecture.

rows.title: Informal Question on optimal directed tree-width constant for regular digraphs

rows.title: Problem 8
rows.paper_title: A note on arithmetic progressions with restricted differences
rows.statement_text: Improve the range of $|S|$ in Theorem 1.
rows.context_text: Theorem 1 establishes that if $q$ is an odd prime power and $S\subseteq\mathbb{F}_{q}$ with $0\in S$ and $|S|>(q+1)/2$, then any $A\subseteq\mathbb{F}_{q}^{n}$ containing no three-term arithmetic progression with common difference in $S^{n}$ satisfies $|A|\leq q^{(1-\varepsilon_{q})n}$. rows.title: Halin's conjecture on hypomorphic infinite graphs
rows.statement_text: If two infinite graphs are hypomorphic, then each is isomorphic to a subgraph of the other.
rows.context_text: Two graphs $G$ and $H$ are hypomorphic if there is a bijection $\varphi\colon V(G)\to V(H)$ with $G - v \cong H - \varphi(v)$ for every vertex $v$. For finite graphs the Reconstruction Conjecture asserts that hypomorphic graphs are isomorphic; this fails for infinite graphs, and Halin's conjecture is the natural weakening.
rows.source_text: If two infinite graphs are hypomorphic, then each is isomorphic to a subgraph of the other.

rows.status_semantics: Halin's conjecture is disproved by Bowler, Erde, Heinig, Lehner, and Pitz (2017). Their Theorem 1.6 constructs two hypomorphic infinite trees T and S with maximum degree 3 such that neither T embeds in S nor S embeds in T, providing an explicit counterexample to the statement that hypomorphic infinite graphs are each isomorphic to a subgraph of the other. The counterexample uses locally finite trees, and the paper explicitly identifies it as a negative answer to Halin's Problem 1.5, which is exactly the conjecture in question.

rows.class_notes: Halin's conjecture: hypomorphic infinite graphs embed in each other; review 2026-09-10 disproved (Bowler-Erde-Heinig-Lehner-Pitz 2017 build two hypomorphic locally finite trees with no embedding either way), so the row is a refutation target, not a proof target.

rows.title: Barát–Thomassen conjecture
rows.statement_text: For every tree $T$ there exists a natural number $k := k(T)$ such that every simple $k$-edge-connected graph whose number of edges is divisible by $e(T)$ admits a decomposition into copies of $T$.
rows.source_text: For every tree $T$ there exists a natural number $k := k(T)$ such that every simple $k$-edge-connected graph whose number of edges is divisible by $e(T)$ admits a decomposition into copies of $T$.

rows.verification_note: Authored in X212.v:barat_thomassen_tree_decomposition_statement. Barat-Thomassen: for every nonempty tree T there is k(T) such that every k(T)-edge-connected simple graph whose edge count is divisible by #|E(T)| decomposes into copies of T. Carrier sgraph; a copy of T is the image edge set x212_copy_edges f of an injective adjacency-preserving f : T -> G (not necessarily induced); the decomposition is a seq of edge sets with count (e in A) over the list equal to (e in E(G)). Library vocabulary: GTBase.common k_edge_connected, sgraph is_tree / E(G). Review 2026-09-10 solved (Bensmail-Harutyunya
rows.status_semantics: The Barát–Thomassen conjecture was proved in full by Bensmail, Harutyunyan, Le, Merker, and Thomassé (2017). They showed that for every tree T on m edges there exists a constant k_T such that every k_T-edge-connected graph whose number of edges is divisible by m can be edge-decomposed into copies of T, confirming exactly the statement as given. The paper appeared in Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B, volume 124 (2017), following an arXiv preprint from March 2016.

rows.status_semantics: Bondy's small cycle double cover conjecture (every bridgeless graph on n vertices has a cycle double cover of size at most n-1) remains open in full generality. Partial results have been established for planar graphs: Jooken, Seamone, and Zamfirescu (2025) prove the bound for planar 4-connected graphs and show every planar 2-connected cubic graph on n > 4 vertices has a CDC of size at most n/2. Notably, the parent CDC conjecture (every bridgeless graph has some cycle double cover) was apparently proved in 2026 via an OpenAI-announced proof with an exposition by Sang-il Oum, but his exposition explicitly notes that Bondy's n-1 bound does not follow immediately from those methods.
rows.class_notes: Bondy's small cycle double cover conjecture: every bridgeless simple graph on n vertices has a cycle double cover with at most n-1 cycles; review 2026-09-10 partial (planar cases only).

rows.title: Linear arboricity conjecture
rows.attributed_to: J. Akiyama, G. Exoo and F. Harary (1981); A.J.W. Hilton (1982)
rows.statement_text: Every simple $k$-regular graph has linear arboricity $\lceil (k+1)/2 \rceil$.
rows.context_text: The linear arboricity $\mathrm{la}(G)$ is the least number of linear forests (forests whose components are paths) whose union is $G$. Equivalently: every simple graph of maximum degree $\Delta$ satisfies $\mathrm{la}(G) \le \lceil (\Delta+1)/2 \rceil$.

rows.status_semantics: The linear arboricity conjecture (la(G) = ⌈(k+1)/2⌉ for every k-regular graph G) remains open in full generality. The conjecture is confirmed for k ≤ 3 (cubic graphs, classical). Best known general upper bound as of 2025 is la(G) ≤ Δ/2 + O(log n) (Christoph et al., 2025), an exponential improvement over the O(Δ^{2/3}) error of Ferber–Fox–Jain (2018). The conjecture is also verified for 2k-regular graphs with girth ≥ 2k (Mishra, 2025).

rows.context_text: By Smith's theorem every edge of a cubic graph lies in an even number of Hamilton cycles, so a second Hamilton cycle always exists; the question is whether one can be found in polynomial time.

rows.status_semantics: The full conjecture — that every 2k-connected graph contains a spanning k-connected bipartite subgraph — remains open, as does Thomassen's more general question of whether any function f(k) independent of n suffices. Delcourt and Ferber (2015) proved f(k,n) ≤ 10^10 k^3 log n (true up to a log n factor), and Yuster (2024) improved this to f(k,n) ≤ 22k^2 log n, reducing the degree in k from cubic to quadratic while the n-dependence remains logarithmic.

Thomassen's 1989 question, as cited in the literature (Delcourt–Ferber 2015), concerns spanning bipartite subgraphs of undirected graphs; the statement above follows that reading. The status review should confirm against the English edition.

rows.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture
rows.statement_text: No graph with more edges than vertices has a thrackle drawing.
rows.context_text: A thrackle is a drawing of a graph in the plane in which every pair of edges meets exactly once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. French: « plongement en manoque ».
rows.source_text: No graph with more edges than vertices has a thrackle drawing.
rows.source_locator: Bondy–Murty Appendix A #31 — Conway's thrackle conjecture — https://inria.hal.science/hal-05211979v1 (book p.629, pdf p.645)

rows.status_semantics: Conway's thrackle conjecture — that no thrackle drawing has more edges than vertices — remains open as of mid-2026. The best known upper bound is approximately 1.393n edges for an n-vertex thrackle, established by Fulek and Pach (journal version 2019). The conjecture has been verified for special classes: linear thrackles (Erdős) and monotone thrackles (Pach and Sterling, 2011). A minimal counterexample, if one exists, would necessarily consist of two even cycles sharing a vertex.
rows.defer_reason: Conway's thrackle conjecture is a statement about drawings in the plane (a thrackle is a drawing in which every pair of edges meets exactly once); no planar-drawing foundation in scope, parked like the other geometry rows (bm_032, bm_054).
rows.class_notes: Conway's thrackle conjecture: no graph with more edges than vertices has a thrackle drawing; review 2026-09-10 partial (Fulek-Pach bound ~1.393n). BLOCKED: a thrackle drawing is a continuous plane drawing, with no finite combinatorial encoding in scope.

rows.status_semantics: Harborth's conjecture — that every simple planar graph has a straight-line planar embedding with all edges of integer length — remains open as of early 2025. The conjecture has been established for several special classes: cubic (3-regular) planar graphs (Geelen, Guo & McKinnon 2008; the stronger integer-coordinate form), some 4-regular planar graphs (Sun 2013), planar 3-trees and maximum-degree-4 graphs (Benediktovich 2013), and additional classes via rigidity-theory constructions (Biedl 2011, Sun 2011). Wikipedia's article on the problem, last updated February 2025, explicitly confirms the general conjecture is unsolved.
rows.defer_reason: Integral straight-line plane drawings: Euclidean/Diophantine geometry, not a finite graph statement; parked as B5 (the planarity side alone would be D6-style).

rows.status_semantics: The Erdős–Sós conjecture (1963) remains open in full generality. Major partial results have appeared: Pokrovskiy (2024) proved the conjecture for all sufficiently large bounded-degree trees; Davoodi, Piguet, Řada, and Sanhueza-Matamala (2026) established an asymptotic version for dense host graphs without any degree restriction on the guest tree; Reed and Stein (2026) proved the conjecture exactly (without approximation) for dense host graphs when k ≥ γn for any fixed γ > 0, also resolving a 51-year-old problem of Erdős and Graham on multicolor Ramsey numbers for trees. The long-announced proof by Ajtai, Komlós, Simonovits, and Szemerédi for sufficiently large k remains unpublished.
rows.class_notes: Erdos-Sos: a simple graph on n vertices with more than n(k-1)/2 edges contains every tree with k edges; review 2026-09-10 partial (Pokrovskiy 2024 large bounded-degree trees; Reed-Stein 2026 exact cases).

rows.title: Even-cycle Turán number
rows.statement_text: For every $k \ge 2$ there is a positive constant $c$ such that $\mathrm{ex}(n, C_{2k}) \ge c\, n^{1+1/k}$.
rows.context_text: $\mathrm{ex}(n, C_{2k})$ is the maximum number of edges of a simple graph on $n$ vertices with no cycle of length $2k$; the Bondy–Simonovits theorem gives the matching upper bound $O(n^{1+1/k})$. Known for $k = 2, 3, 5$.

READBACK 2026-09-23 (second reader): PASS. p^k*n^(k+1) <= q^k*m^k is exactly m >= (p/q)*n^(1+1/k) after clearing, and the existential lower-bound form is equivalent to a lower bound on the (undefined) maximum. Not v
rows.status_semantics: The conjecture that ex(n, C_{2k}) >= c * n^{1+1/k} for all k >= 2 remains open in general. The lower bound is established only for k = 2 (via polarity graphs giving Theta(n^{3/2})), k = 3 (incidence graphs of projective planes giving Theta(n^{4/3})), and k = 5 (related to generalized hexagons, giving Theta(n^{6/5})). For all other k, the best known general lower bound is the Lazebnik–Ustimenko–Woldar construction (1995) yielding ex(n, C_{2k}) >= c * n^{1 + 2/(3k-3)}, which falls short of the conjectured n^{1+1/k}. No recent breakthrough resolving the conjecture for all k was found in a thorough search through 2026.
rows.class_notes: Even-cycle Turan number: for every k >= 2 there is c > 0 with ex(n, C_2k) >= c n^(1+1/k); review 2026-09-10 partial (known only for k = 2, 3, 5). The n^(1+1/k) growth is asymptotic.

rows.status_semantics: The existence of the limit $\lim_{k\to\infty} r(k,k)^{1/k}$ remains open. The lower bound gives $\liminf_{k\to\infty} r(k,k)^{1/k} \ge \sqrt{2}$ (Erd\u0151s 1947, sharpened by Spencer). In 2023, Campos, Griffiths, Morris, and Sahasrabudhe proved $r(k,k) \le (4-\varepsilon)^k$ for $\varepsilon = 2^{-7}$, the first exponential improvement over the 1935 Erd\u0151s\u2013Szekeres upper bound of $4^k$; a 2024 preprint reportedly pushed the upper bound further to approximately $3.799^k$. Neither result resolves whether the limit exists or determines its value.

Checked tight at k = 3 (T = K_{1,
rows.status_semantics: The specific conjecture r(T,T) ≤ 2n−2 for all trees T on n vertices appears to remain open. The related general Burr–Erdős conjecture — that r(H,H) is linear in n for any fixed degeneracy d (trees are 1-degenerate) — was proven by Choongbum Lee (2017, Annals of Mathematics), establishing r(T,T) = O(n). However, Lee's theorem gives a constant c_1 that is not claimed to equal 2, so the specific upper bound 2n−2 is not settled by this proof. The bound is known to be tight: stars K_{1,n−1} achieve r(K_{1,n−1}, K_{1,n−1}) = 2n−2.

rows.title: Erdős–Lovász Tihany conjecture
rows.statement_text: Let $G$ be a $k$-chromatic graph containing no $k$-clique, and let $k + 1 = k_1 + k_2$ with $k_1, k_2 \ge 2$. Then $G$ has vertex-disjoint subgraphs $G_1$ and $G_2$ such that $G_i$ is $k_i$-chromatic, $i = 1, 2$.
rows.source_text: Let $G$ be a $k$-chromatic graph containing no $k$-clique, and let $k + 1 = k_1 + k_2$ with $k_1, k_2 \ge 2$. Then $G$ has vertex-disjoint subgraphs $G_1$ and $G_2$ such that $G_i$ is $k_i$-chromatic, $i = 1, 2$.

rows.verification_note: Authored in X213.v:erdos_lovasz_tihany_statement. Erdos-Lovasz Tihany (Bondy-Murty A.45): a graph with chi(G) = k and every clique smaller than k splits into two DISJOINT vertex sets of chromatic numbers exactly k1 and k2 whenever k+1 = k1+k2 with k1, k2 >= 2; the source's 'vertex-disjoint subgraphs' is read as induced subgraphs (chi(A) is the chromatic number of the subgraph induced on A), which is equivalent.
rows.status_semantics: The Erdős–Lovász Tihany conjecture (Lovász 1968) remains open in full generality as of 2026. Substantial partial progress has been made: Stiebitz (1987, pre-2008) proved the case k₁=2 for all k₂; subsequent work has confirmed the conjecture for claw-free graphs (Chudnovsky–Fradkin–Plumettaz 2013), for graphs with forbidden holes (Song 2018), for line graphs of multigraphs and for graphs with independence number two (Wang–Yu 2020), and most recently for all even-hole-free graphs (Song 2026). The general statement for arbitrary k-chromatic triangle-free-in-clique graphs is still open.
rows.class_notes: Erdos-Lovasz Tihany: a k-chromatic K_k-free graph splits off vertex-disjoint k_1- and k_2-chromatic subgraphs whenever k+1 = k_1+k_2 with k_i >= 2; review 2026-09-10 partial (k_1 = 2 by Stiebitz; claw-free and line-graph cases).

El-Zahar-Erdos (Bondy-Murty A.46): one function f of (r,k), quantified before the graphs, such that chi(G) >= f(r,k) forces either an r-clique or an ANTICOMPLETE pair of vertex sets each of chromatic number exactly k (X3's x3_anticomplete), i.e. an induced subgraph that is the disjoint union of two k-chromatic graphs.
rows.status_semantics: The El-Zahar–Erdős conjecture (1985/1986) asks whether every graph with chromatic number at least f(r,k) must contain either an r-clique or an induced subgraph that is the disjoint union of two k-chromatic graphs (equivalently, two anticomplete subgraphs each with chromatic number at least k). The full conjecture remains open. Nguyen, Scott, and Seymour (2023) proved a weaker variant: for all t, c ≥ 1 there exists d such that if χ(G) ≥ d and ω(G) < t, then G has anticomplete subgraphs A, B where one has minimum degree at least c and the other has chromatic number at least c—but not both chromatic number at least c as the conjecture requires. The problem was still listed as open at the Barbados 2025 Graph Theory Workshop.
rows.class_notes: El-Zahar-Erdos: is there f(r,k) such that chi(G) >= f(r,k) forces an r-clique or an induced disjoint union of two k-chromatic graphs? Review 2026-09-10 partial (Nguyen-Scott-Seymour 2023 prove a weaker variant). Carries an 'exists f' wrapper.

rows.status_semantics: The conjecture that every triangle-free graph of infinite chromatic number contains every finite tree as an induced subgraph remains open in general. It follows from the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture (item 49), which is itself open. Partial results are known: Martin (2016) proved that certain radius-three trees appear as induced subgraphs in radius-two triangle-free graphs of sufficiently large chromatic number, establishing the conjecture for this restricted class of graphs and trees. No full resolution has been found in the literature.
rows.class_notes: Gyarfas: every triangle-free graph of INFINITE chromatic number contains every finite tree as an induced subgraph; review 2026-09-10 partial (follows from the open Gyarfas-Sumner conjecture; radius-three cases known). Infinite chromatic number needs infinite graphs.

rows.title: Chromatic number of the plane (Hadwiger–Nelson problem)
rows.statement_text: Determine the chromatic number of the unit-distance graph of the plane, i.e. the least number of colours needed to colour the points of $\mathbb{R}^2$ so that no two points at distance $1$ receive the same colour.
rows.context_text: At the time of the book, $4 \le \chi(\mathbb{R}^2) \le 7$.

rows.status_semantics: The exact chromatic number of the plane remains unknown. De Grey (2018) improved the lower bound from 4 to 5 by constructing a 1581-vertex unit-distance graph that is not 4-colourable, so the current range is 5 ≤ χ(ℝ²) ≤ 7. Subsequent work (Heule 2018, Polymath16 2021) reduced the smallest known witness to 509 vertices, but no progress on the upper bound has been made. For the map-type colouring variant (regions bounded by non-unit-circle arcs with trivalent vertices), Sokolov–Voronov (2025) proved a lower bound of 7, but this does not settle the point-colouring formulation.
rows.notes: Editorial lead, to be confirmed by the status review: de Grey (2018) showed the chromatic number is at least 5.

rows.title: 1-factorization conjecture
rows.statement_text: Every simple $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices with $n$ even and $d \ge n/2$ is $d$-edge-colourable.
rows.context_text: Equivalently, such graphs have a 1-factorization. Usually stated (Chetwynd and Hilton 1985) with the sharper threshold $d \ge 2\lceil n/4 \rceil - 1$.
rows.source_text: Every simple $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices with $n$ even and $d \ge n/2$ is $d$-edge-colourable.

rows.status_semantics: The 1-factorization conjecture has been proved for all sufficiently large n by Csaba, Kühn, Lo, Osthus, and Treglown in a landmark paper published in Memoirs of the American Mathematical Society 244 (2016). Their result establishes that every simple d-regular graph on n even vertices with d ≥ n/2 is d-edge-colourable, provided n exceeds an unspecified absolute constant. The conjecture in full generality—covering all even n with no lower bound on n—remains open.

rows.title: Vizing's interchange conjecture
rows.statement_text: Given a proper edge colouring of a graph $G$, a proper edge colouring of $G$ with $\chi'(G)$ colours can be obtained by a sequence of colour interchanges on alternating paths or cycles (Kempe changes).
rows.source_text: Given a proper edge colouring of a graph $G$, a proper edge colouring of $G$ with $\chi'(G)$ colours can be obtained by a sequence of colour interchanges on alternating paths or cycles (Kempe changes).

rows.verification_note: Authored in X213.v:vizing_kempe_interchange_statement. Vizing's interchange conjecture (Bondy-Murty A.60), corpus status SOLVED (Narboni 2023): from every proper k-edge-colouring a colouring using at most m colours is reachable by Kempe changes, for every achievable m <= k -- which avoids naming chi'(G), the least such m. A Kempe change interchanges two colours on a line-adjacency-CLOSED set of two-coloured edges (a union of alternating paths and cycles); reachability is a nat-indexed Fixpoint.
rows.status_semantics: Narboni (arXiv:2302.12914, February 2023) proves the full statement: starting from any proper edge colouring of a graph G, one can reach an optimal (Δ-edge) colouring by a sequence of Kempe changes, provided such a colouring exists. This resolves Vizing's 1965 conjecture for all graphs. A precursor result by Bonamy, Defrain, Klimošová, Lagoutte, and Narboni (arXiv:2107.07900) had established the conjecture for the special case of triangle-free graphs, published in J. Combin. Theory Ser. B (2023). As of this review, Narboni's general proof remains an arXiv preprint without verified journal publication, hence confidence is medium rather than high.
rows.notes: Editorial lead, to be confirmed by the status review: Narboni, 'Vizing's edge-recoloring conjecture holds' (arXiv:2302.12914, 2023); triangle-free case by Bonamy, Defrain, Klimošová, Lagoutte and Narboni (J. Combin. Theory Ser. B, 2023).

rows.status_semantics: Kotzig's conjecture asserts that for k ≥ 3 no finite graph (called a P_k-graph or k-graph) exists in which every pair of vertices is connected by exactly one path of length k. The conjecture has been verified for all k ≤ 20 by Kostochka (1988), who also claimed—without publishing a proof—that his techniques extend to k ≤ 33. Ma and Zhao (2025) established an Ω(k^{2/3}) lower bound on the intersection size for general k-connected graphs, and Chen (2026) further improved this to Ω(k^{8/11}) via a forbidden-subdivision approach.

rows.title: Birmelé's conjecture on long cycles
rows.statement_text: If any two cycles of length at least $k$ in a graph intersect, then the graph has a set of $k$ vertices meeting every cycle of length at least $k$.
rows.source_text: If any two cycles of length at least $k$ in a graph intersect, then the graph has a set of $k$ vertices meeting every cycle of length at least $k$.

rows.verification_note: Authored in X212.v:birmele_long_cycle_transversal_statement. Birmele-Bondy-Reed: if any two cycles on at least k vertices meet, then some set of AT MOST k vertices meets every cycle on at least k vertices. The guard 3 <= k is load-bearing: for k <= 2 the hypothesis only says that any two cycles meet, which holds in K_5, while no single vertex or pair meets all cycles of K_5, so the unguarded statement is false; the conjecture is posed for k >= 3. 'A set of k vertices' is read as at most k (a set of exactly k vertices need not exist when #|G| < k).
rows.status_semantics: The conjecture is known in the literature as the Birmelé–Bondy–Reed conjecture: every graph without two vertex-disjoint cycles of length at least ℓ has a set of at most ℓ vertices meeting all cycles of length at least ℓ. It remains open. A sequence of papers has improved the bound: Birmelé–Bondy–Reed proved 2ℓ+3 vertices suffice; Meierling–Rautenbach–Sasse improved this to 5ℓ/3+29/2; Ma and Zu (2021) further improved to 3ℓ/2+7/2. No resolution was found in papers from 2022–2026.

rows.status_semantics: The Matthews–Sumner conjecture (every 4-connected claw-free graph is Hamiltonian, 1984) remains open as of September 2026. Via Ryjáček's 1997 closure theorem it is equivalent to Thomassen's conjecture that every 4-connected line graph is Hamiltonian, also open. The strongest known partial result is Kaiser and Vrána (2012), who proved that every 5-connected line graph of minimum degree at least 6 is Hamiltonian, improving the previous threshold from 7-connected. A 2026 paper by Ozeki and Zhang addresses Hamiltonicity in 3-connected claw-free graphs with small domination number, motivated by Thomassen's conjecture, but does not resolve the 4-connected case.
rows.class_notes: Matthews-Sumner: every 4-connected claw-free graph is Hamiltonian; review 2026-09-10 partial (equivalent to Thomassen's line-graph conjecture; Kaiser-Vrana 2012 for 5-connected line graphs of min degree >= 6).

rows.title: Chvátal's toughness conjecture
rows.statement_text: There exists a positive integer $k$ such that every $k$-tough graph is Hamiltonian.
rows.context_text: A graph $G$ is $t$-tough if $|S| \ge t \cdot c(G - S)$ for every vertex cut $S$, where $c(\cdot)$ counts components. French: « k-endurant ».
rows.source_text: There exists a positive integer $k$ such that every $k$-tough graph is Hamiltonian.

rows.verification_note: Authored in X211.v:chvatal_toughness_hamiltonian_statement. Chvatal's toughness conjecture: exists a positive integer k such that every k-tough graph on more than two vertices is Hamiltonian. Toughness is rational-free in the cleared form [k * #|components (~: S)| <= #|S|] for every S leaving at least two components (library [components]). The guard 2 < #|G| is load-bearing and proved to have teeth in grounding_X211.v ('K_1 is vacuously k-tough for every k and is not Hamiltonian under GTBase.common's cycle convention).
rows.status_semantics: Chvátal's toughness conjecture remains open in full generality as of September 2026. If the conjecture is true, the constant k must satisfy k ≥ 9/4 (a lower bound from Bauer, Broersma, and Veldman via non-Hamiltonian (9/4−ε)-tough graphs). The conjecture has been verified for several special graph classes: chordal graphs (k=10 suffices, Kabela–Kaiser 2015), claw-free graphs, planar graphs, and various forbidden-subgraph-free families addressed in a sequence of recent papers through 2026. No counterexample to the general existential statement is known, and no proof for general graphs has been found.
rows.class_notes: Chvatal's toughness conjecture: some k makes every k-tough graph Hamiltonian; review 2026-09-10 partial (k >= 9/4 necessary; chordal, claw-free and planar cases known). Needs toughness, stated in the integral t*k form to stay rational-free.

Thomassen's question 'is there a hypohamiltonian graph of minimum degree at least 4?', formalised as the existence statement it asks about: exists G with every degree >= 4 that is not Hamiltonian while every vertex-deleted subgraph [induced ([set: G] :\ v)] is. Minimum degree >= 4 forces #|G| >= 5, so no vertex-deleted subgraph is a digon and the cycle convention is inert. An exhaustive search over all graphs on at most 7 vertices found no witness (consistent with the row's open status).

rows.title: Grötschel's conjecture on bipartite hypotraceable graphs

rows.context_text: A graph is hypotraceable if it has no Hamilton path but every vertex-deleted subgraph has one.

rows.title: Antichain Coverage Conjecture (refuted at n=12)
rows.statement_text: Definitions as in the Universal Replacement Conjecture row (2-pole side (H,(r1,r2)), port states, boundary trace, Trace(H,(r1,r2))). Consider the finite family L10 = {Trace(H',(s1,s2)) : (H',(s1,s2)) a 2-pole side with |V(H')| ≤ 10} (the n≤10 gadget lattice; 59 distinct trace sets), and let its ⊆-minimal elements be the 7 minimal trace classes (class ids C0, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7; minimum realising orders 4, 10, 10, 10, 6, 8, 8; a mutually ⊆-incomparable antichain whose union is the full 16-trace universe; archived in data/gadget_lattice_2pole_n10_both.json). REFUTED CLAIM: for every 2-pole side (H,(r1,r2)) with |V(H)| ≥ 4, at least one of these 7 minimal trace sets is a subset of Trace(H,(r1,r2)). (Equivalently, in the folder's wording: every realisable 2-pole trace set contains a minimal lattice trace set — which would have made every side of order > 10 trace-replaceable by a minimal-class gadget and closed Lemma 2 from the n≤10 lattice alone.)

rows.title: Core Absorption Lemma (all-orders form)
rows.statement_text: Definitions as in the Universal Replacement Conjecture row (2-pole side, port states, Trace, compatibility-universal), plus: a 3-decomposition of a connected cubic (3-regular simple) graph G is a partition E(G)=T⊔C⊔M with T a spanning tree, C a 2-regular subgraph (every vertex of C has degree exactly 2 in C; possibly empty), M a matching (possibly empty); a 2-edge-cut F={e1,e2} of G is essential iff the four endpoints of e1,e2 are pairwise distinct; its sides are the two components of G−F, each a 2-pole side whose ports are the two cut-edge endpoints it contains. CONJECTURE. Let G be a connected cubic simple graph with no 3-decomposition and with |V(G)| minimum among such graphs (a smallest counterexample), let F={e1,e2} be an essential 2-edge-cut of G, and let H be a side of F with ports (a1,a2). Then at least one of: (a) H contains a bridge that is also a bridge of G; (b) H contains a bridge e* such that {e1,e*} or {e2,e*} is an essential 2-edge-cut of G whose smaller side has strictly fewer vertices than the smaller side of F; (c) Trace(H,(a1,a2)) contains, as a subset, at least one of the ten explicit core trace sets C0, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, C7, C8, C22, C23 of the n≤12 gadget lattice (each a concrete finite trace set realised by a specific 2-pole side on at most 12 vertices, archived in data/gadget_lattice_2pole_n12_both.json and data/n14_absorbing_core.json; e.g. C0 = the diamond K4-minus-edge set {(T_CC,T_T) split, (T_T,T_CC) split, (T_TM,T_TM) joined}); (d) Trace(H,(a1,a2)) is compatibility-universal.

rows.title: Lemma C — essentially-3-connected C0/compatibility dichotomy
rows.statement_text: Definitions as in the Universal Replacement Conjecture row: 2-pole side (H,(r1,r2)) (connected simple max-degree-3 graph, exactly two degree-2 ports r1 ≠ r2, all other vertices degree 3); port states T_T=(T;{T,T}), T_TM=(T;{T,M}), M_TT=(M;{T,T}), T_CC=(T;{C,C}), C_TC=(C;{T,C}); boundary trace (χ,π) and Trace(H,(r1,r2)) defined via partitions E(H)=T_H⊔C_H⊔M_H with C_H a disjoint union of cycles, M_H a matching, T_H acyclic, side-edge colours at each port matching χ, every component of (V(H),T_H) containing a boundary-T port, and π the partition of boundary-T ports by T_H-component; compatibility-universal = Trace contains all four axis types (TT-joined, TT-split, (T,M), (M,T)). Call (H,(r1,r2)) essentially 3-connected iff H has no bridge and no cut vertex, and every 2-element vertex set whose removal disconnects H equals the neighbourhood N(r1) or N(r2) of a port. Let Trace(C0) denote the 3-element trace set of the diamond gadget K4-minus-an-edge (graph6 'C^', ports its two degree-2 vertices): {(T_CC,T_T) with π={{r1},{r2}}, (T_T,T_CC) with π={{r1},{r2}}, (T_TM,T_TM) with π={{r1,r2}}}. CONJECTURE. For every essentially-3-connected 2-pole side (H,(r1,r2)) with |V(H)| ≥ 4, either Trace(C0) ⊆ Trace(H,(r1,r2)), or Trace(H,(r1,r2)) is compatibility-universal.

rows.title: Cycle-bypass lemma (Lemma C piece 1)
rows.statement_text: With the same definitions as the Lemma C row (2-pole side, port states, Trace, essentially 3-connected): for every essentially-3-connected 2-pole side (H,(r1,r2)) with |V(H)| ≥ 4, both bypass traces are realisable, i.e. (T_CC,T_T) with π={{r1},{r2}} ∈ Trace(H,(r1,r2)) and (T_T,T_CC) with π={{r1},{r2}} ∈ Trace(H,(r1,r2)). Concretely, for each i ∈ {1,2} there is a partition E(H)=T_H⊔C_H⊔M_H in which C_H is a vertex-disjoint union of cycles one of which passes through r_i using both of r_i's H-edges, the other port has both its H-edges in T_H, M_H is a matching, T_H is acyclic, and every component of (V(H),T_H) contains a boundary-T port (r_i forming its own singleton T-component).

rows.title: Target theorem — minimal counterexample is 3-edge-connected
rows.statement_text: A 3-decomposition of a connected cubic (3-regular simple) graph G is a partition E(G) = T ⊔ C ⊔ M where T is a spanning tree of G, C is a 2-regular subgraph (every vertex of C has degree exactly 2 in C; possibly empty), and M is a matching (possibly empty). CONJECTURE (target theorem of the attack). Every connected cubic simple graph G that admits no 3-decomposition and has minimum |V(G)| among all connected cubic simple graphs admitting no 3-decomposition is 3-edge-connected (no set of at most 2 edges disconnects G). (This implies the non-vacuous reduction: if any connected cubic graph lacks a 3-decomposition, then some 3-edge-connected one does.)

rows.title: Sub-lemma 1' (subcubic existence at a bridge port)
rows.statement_text: Let H be a connected simple graph of maximum degree 3 with exactly one vertex r of degree 2, every other vertex having degree exactly 3 (a 1-pole side whose unique port r has port-degree 1). Then there exists a partition E(H) = T_H ⊔ C_H ⊔ M_H such that: T_H is a spanning tree of H; every vertex incident to an edge of C_H has exactly two C_H-edges (C_H is a vertex-disjoint union of cycles, possibly empty); M_H is a matching (possibly empty); and at r either (port state T_T) both H-edges at r are in T_H, i.e. deg_{T_H}(r)=2 and deg_{C_H}(r)=deg_{M_H}(r)=0, or (port state T_TM) one H-edge at r is in T_H and the other is in M_H, i.e. deg_{T_H}(r)=1, deg_{M_H}(r)=1, deg_{C_H}(r)=0.

rows.title: Simple-swap universality hypothesis (refuted at n=14)
rows.statement_text: Definitions as in the Lemma C row (2-pole side, port states, Trace, essentially 3-connected; Trace(C0) = the diamond trace set). A (T_TM,T_TM)-split partition of a 2-pole side (H,(r1,r2)) is a partition E(H)=T_H⊔C_H⊔M_H realising the trace (T_TM,T_TM) with π={{r1},{r2}}: each port has one inside T_H-edge and one inside M_H-edge (boundary colour T), C_H is a disjoint union of cycles, M_H a matching, and T_H has exactly two components, A containing r1 and B containing r2. For i∈{1,2} let w_i be the M_H-neighbour of r_i. REFUTED CLAIM (working hypothesis behind the simple-swap route to the M-axis dichotomy): every one of the 7 unoriented essentially-3-connected 2-pole sides at |V(H)|=14 with Trace(C0) ⊄ Trace(H) (the n=14 C0-exception graphs) admits at least one (T_TM,T_TM)-split partition in which simultaneously w_1 ∈ B and w_2 ∈ A — the configuration under which the simple double edge-swap (recolour each port's inside M-edge to T and its boundary half-edge to M) yields realisations of both M-axis traces (M_TT,T_T) and (T_T,M_TT) without creating a cycle in T_H.

rows.title: Universal Replacement Conjecture
rows.statement_text: Definitions. A 2-pole side is a pair (H,(r1,r2)) where H is a connected simple graph of maximum degree 3 with exactly two vertices r1 ≠ r2 of degree 2 (the ports), all other vertices of degree exactly 3 (this is exactly the form of a side of an essential 2-edge-cut of a cubic graph). The five port states are pairs (boundary colour; multiset of colours of the port's two H-edges): T_T=(T;{T,T}), T_TM=(T;{T,M}), M_TT=(M;{T,T}), T_CC=(T;{C,C}), C_TC=(C;{T,C}). A boundary trace is a pair (χ,π) where χ assigns a port state to each port and π is a partition of the set of ports whose χ-boundary colour is T. (χ,π) ∈ Trace(H,(r1,r2)) iff there is a partition E(H) = T_H ⊔ C_H ⊔ M_H with: (i) every vertex incident to C_H has exactly two C_H-edges (C_H a vertex-disjoint union of cycles); (ii) M_H a matching; (iii) T_H acyclic; (iv) at each port the multiset of colours of its two H-edges equals the side-colour multiset of its χ-state; (v) every connected component of the spanning subgraph (V(H),T_H) (isolated vertices allowed) contains at least one port of χ-boundary colour T; (vi) two boundary-T ports are in the same block of π iff they are in the same component of (V(H),T_H). Trace(H,(r1,r2)) is compatibility-universal iff it contains traces of all four axis types: both boundary colours T with π={{r1,r2}} (joined); both boundary colours T with π={{r1},{r2}} (split); boundary colours (T,M); boundary colours (M,T). (By the folder's proved Theorem 3.14 this is equivalent to: every trace τ in the 16-element universe U of realisable 2-pole traces is boundary-compatible with some σ ∈ Trace(H,(r1,r2)).) CONJECTURE. For every 2-pole side (H,(r1,r2)) with |V(H)| ≥ 12, at least one of: (a) there exists a 2-pole side (H0,(s1,s2)) with |V(H0)| < |V(H)| and Trace(H0,(s1,s2)) ⊆ Trace(H,(r1,r2)) (H is trace-contained by a strictly smaller gadget class, hence Lemma-2-replaceable); or (b) Trace(H,(r1,r2)) is compatibility-universal.

rows.title: B2: 2-separable + diam >= 4 + D2 < n implies BIGTORSO >= n
rows.statement_text: Let G be a finite 2-connected simple graph with diam(G) >= 4 that has a 2-vertex cut (is not 3-connected) and satisfies D2(G) < |V(G)| (D2 as in row B1). Then BIGTORSO(G) >= |V(G)|. Definition: for every pair {a,b} whose removal disconnects G and every connected component C of G - {a,b}, the torso is the edge-weighted graph on C u {a,b} consisting of all edges of G inside C u {a,b} with weight 1, plus, if ab is not an edge of G, a virtual edge ab whose weight equals the distance from a to b in the induced subgraph of G on V(G) \ C (which contains a and b). Lines of the torso are defined by the same betweenness rule applied to the torso's weighted shortest-path metric, and ell(torso) counts its distinct lines; BIGTORSO(G) := max of ell(torso) over all such 2-cuts {a,b} and components C.

rows.title: Lemma A easy-branch residual: D' >= excess for marked 2-connected graphs
rows.statement_text: Let B be a finite 2-connected simple graph, u in V(B) a marked vertex, S := V(B) \ {u}, d the shortest-path metric of B. Write x <= y iff d(u,x) + d(x,y) = d(u,y). For s in S set Sigma_s := {x in S : x <= s or s <= x}, F_s := {x in S : d(x,u) + d(u,s) = d(x,s)}, and the apex trace A_s := Sigma_s u F_s. Partition S into fibers by the value of Sigma_s; in each fiber designate as representative the member of minimum depth d(u,.), ties broken by smallest vertex index; the remaining members are non-representatives. Put a := #{A_s : s a non-representative}, excess := (#non-representatives) - a, and D' := #{ line_B(x,y) : x != y in V(B), u not in line_B(x,y), line_B(x,y) != S } (the u-avoiding proper lines of B, lines as in row H5). Claim: D' >= excess.

rows.title: Lemma A: leaf-block amalgam inequality (non-2-connected case of H5)
rows.statement_text: Let G be a finite connected simple graph with no vertex of degree 1, diam(G) >= 4, and at least one cut vertex (not 2-connected). Let B be any leaf block of G (a maximal 2-connected subgraph containing exactly one cut vertex u of G; pendant-freeness forces every leaf block to be a non-bridge block with |V(B)| >= 3), S := V(B) \ {u}, and R := G - S (the induced subgraph on V(G) \ S; it is connected and contains u). Then ell(G) >= |S| + max(ell(R), |R|), where lines/ell are as in row H5 and ell(R) is computed in R with R's own shortest-path metric. This inequality implies ell(G) >= |V(G)| for every non-2-connected H5 input (the max term self-compensates any line-deficit of R; no induction on R needed).

rows.statement_text: The lexicographic substitution product G_2[G_2] belongs to the class C_3, where G_2 is the directed triangle on {0,1,2} with arcs 0->1, 1->2, 2->0, and G_2[G_2] is the 9-vertex digraph on vertex set {0,1,2} x {0,1,2} with intra-block arcs (i,u)->(i,v) for every i and every arc u->v of G_2, plus ALL nine inter-block arcs (i,u)->(j,v) for every arc i->j of G_2; C_3 = oriented digraphs (no digon) with no transitive triangle TT3 (no distinct u,v,w with arcs u->v, v->w, u->w) and no induced directed cycle of length >= 4. (Membership would make G_2[G_2] a 9-vertex C_3 digraph with dichromatic number 3, i.e. m(3) <= 9.)

rows.title: Directed-degeneracy threshold N(3) >= 10 (disproved: cyclic K_{3,3,3})
rows.statement_text: Every digraph D on at most 9 vertices in the class C_3 (oriented, no digon; no transitive triangle TT3, i.e. no distinct u,v,w with arcs u->v, v->w, u->w; no induced directed cycle of length >= 4) has directed degeneracy dd(D) <= 2, where dd(D) := max over induced subdigraphs H of D of min over v in V(H) of min(d+_H(v), d-_H(v)) (d+/d- = out-/in-degree in H). Equivalently N(3) >= 10, where N(t) := min{ |V(D)| : D in C_3 and dd(D) >= t }. (This was the falsifiable prediction of the route conjecturing N(t) super-linear, aiming at an asymptotic lower bound m(k) >= N(k-1) via the sound inequality chi_vec <= 1 + dd.)

rows.title: Lemma L: chi_vec <= omega(underlying) - 1 on C_3 (disproved: edgeless digraph)
rows.statement_text: For every digraph D in the class C_3 (oriented, no digon; no transitive triangle TT3, i.e. no distinct u,v,w with arcs u->v, v->w, u->w; no induced directed cycle of length >= 4), the dichromatic number satisfies chi_vec(D) <= omega(U(D)) - 1, where U(D) is the underlying simple graph of D (edge {u,v} present iff u->v or v->u is an arc of D), omega denotes the clique number, and chi_vec(D) is the least k such that V(D) partitions into k parts each inducing an acyclic subdigraph.

rows.title: Small 3-dichromatic C_3 witness: m(3) <= 20
rows.statement_text: There exists a digraph D on at most 20 vertices such that (i) D is oriented (no loops and no digons: never both arcs u->v and v->u), (ii) D contains no transitive triangle TT3 (no three distinct vertices u,v,w with all three arcs u->v, v->w, u->w), (iii) D contains no induced directed cycle of length >= 4 (no vertex subset S with |S| >= 4 whose induced subdigraph is exactly a directed cycle on S) -- i.e. D belongs to the class C_3 of arXiv:2202.01006 -- and (iv) the dichromatic number chi_vec(D) >= 3, where chi_vec(D) is the least k such that V(D) can be partitioned into k parts each inducing an acyclic subdigraph. Equivalently, m(3) <= 20, where m(k) := min{ |V(D)| : D in C_3 and chi_vec(D) >= k }.

rows.title: Ore-corner certification at (26,51): every 26-Ore graph on 51 vertices has cr >= Z(26) = 5148
rows.statement_text: For a finite simple graph G, let cr(G) denote the crossing number: the minimum, over all drawings of G in the plane (vertices as distinct points, edges as arcs, no three edges through a common interior point), of the number of pairs of edges that cross. Let O_26 be the smallest class of graphs containing K_26 and closed under DHGO (Ore) composition with k = 26: given G1, G2 in O_k, an edge xy in E(G1) whose endpoint y has deg_{G1}(y) = k-1, a vertex z in V(G2) with deg_{G2}(z) = k-1, and a partition N_{G2}(z) = A ⊔ B with A, B nonempty, the composition G1 * G2 is obtained from the disjoint union of G1 - xy and (G2 - z) by adding the edges {xa : a in A} and {yb : b in B} (so |V(G1 * G2)| = |V(G1)| + |V(G2)| - 1; the vertices of A and B remain distinct). CLAIM: every G in O_26 with |V(G)| = 51 satisfies cr(G) >= 5148, where 5148 = Z(26) := (1/4)·floor(26/2)·floor(25/2)·floor(24/2)·floor(23/2) = 13·12·12·11/4 (Guy–Zarankiewicz quantity). Finite handle: by the D4 enumeration (in-folder, pynauty-canonical-form certified), O_26 restricted to 51 vertices is exactly the 12 pairwise non-isomorphic one-step compositions K_26 * K_26 parameterised by the partition size |A| = a in {1,...,12}, stored as graph6 lines in deliverables/D4_ore_26_51/ore_26_51.g6 (each with 51 vertices, 649 edges, minimum degree 25); the claim is a conjunction of 12 decidable statements cr(O_a) >= 5148.

rows.title: List-chromatic Albertson at t <= 18 (D15 main theorem / D14 T1'; refuted at t = 5)
rows.statement_text: For every finite simple graph G and every integer t with 1 <= t <= 18: if chi_l(G) >= t then cr(G) >= cr(K_t). Here chi_l(G) (list-chromatic / choice number) is the least k such that for every assignment of colour lists L(v) with |L(v)| = k for every vertex v, G admits a proper colouring c with c(v) in L(v) for all v; cr is the crossing number (minimum number of edge-pair crossings over plane drawings). DISPROVED at the instance t = 5: Voigt (1993) constructs a planar graph G_V that is not 4-choosable; planar graphs are 5-choosable (Thomassen 1994), so chi_l(G_V) = 5, while cr(G_V) = 0 < 1 = cr(K_5).

rows.title: FPS Claim 3.7 free-delta improvement (D5 headline: some delta beats 9/16; refuted by D8 witness identity)
rows.statement_text: Define f(alpha, beta, gamma; delta) := gamma - alpha·(delta - 1)/(delta - gamma), and for delta in (1, 5/4) let F(delta) := sup { f(alpha, beta, gamma; delta) : 0 <= alpha <= beta <= 1, 0 <= gamma <= alpha + (delta - alpha)(1 - beta)/(2 - beta) } — the Fox–Pach–Suk Claim 3.7 optimisation (arXiv:2510.05893, p. 9) with the degree-threshold parameter delta freed (FPS prove F(9/8) = 9/16; the admissible range (1, 5/4) comes from FPS Claim 3.6's hypothesis 4d < 5k). REFUTED CLAIM (D5 headline, from the D3 §7 re-tuning hypothesis): there exists delta in (1, 5/4) with F(delta) < 9/16 — specifically F(delta_1) ≈ 0.557454 at delta_1 ≈ 1.114907, the root in (1, 5/4) of delta^3 + 3·delta^2 - delta - 4 = 0. DISPROOF (D8 Theorem 1): F(delta) >= 9/16 for every delta in (1, 5/4), with equality iff delta = 9/8; the load-bearing certificate is the witness identity f_2b(4/7, delta) - 9/16 = 12·(delta - 9/8)^2 / [7·(4·delta - 1)] = 3·(8·delta - 9)^2 / [112·(4·delta - 1)] >= 0, where f_2b(eta, delta) is f evaluated at the explicit feasible point alpha = beta = 2 - 1/eta, gamma = alpha + (delta - alpha)(1 - beta)/(2 - beta) (the Case-2b boundary; at eta = 4/7: alpha = beta = 1/4). The refuted claim rested on the silent assumption that the Case-2b maximum equals delta/2 at every delta, which fails on (1, -3 + sqrt(17)) ∋ delta_1 (monotonicity transition at delta_crit = -3 + sqrt(17) ≈ 1.12311).

rows.title: 25-Ore family at (25,48) is nonempty (Role 2 claim '12 Ore classes / essentially a single graph'; refuted by Ore-order congruence)
rows.statement_text: There exists a graph G in O_25 with |V(G)| = 48, where O_25 is the smallest class of graphs containing K_25 and closed under DHGO (Ore) composition with k = 25 (composition as defined in Kostochka–Yancey arXiv:1209.1050 §2: pick xy in E(G1) with deg_{G1}(y) = 24, z in V(G2) with deg_{G2}(z) = 24, partition N_{G2}(z) = A ⊔ B nonempty, delete xy and z, add edges {xa : a in A} and {yb : b in B}; |V(G1 * G2)| = |V(G1)| + |V(G2)| - 1). DISPROVED: every G in O_k satisfies |V(G)| ≡ 1 (mod k - 1), by induction on the composition tree (base case |V(K_k)| = k ≡ 1 mod k-1; the composition step preserves the congruence since n1 + n2 - 1 ≡ 1 + 1 - 1 = 1 mod k-1); for k = 25 this forces |V| in {25, 49, 73, ...}, and 48 ≡ 0 (mod 24) ≠ 1. In particular K_25 * K_25 has order 49, not 48; the 25-Ore family on 48 vertices is empty.

rows.title: Delta = 4 case of Cheng-Keevash Conjecture 1 (full closure at all n)
rows.statement_text: Let D = (V, A) be a finite digraph (A a set of ordered pairs of distinct vertices; write u -> v for (u,v) in A). D is an oriented graph if for no pair of distinct vertices u, v both u -> v and v -> u are arcs (no 2-cycles). For v in V, d+(v) is the number of arcs with tail v, and delta+(D) := min_{v in V} d+(v). A directed path of length k is a sequence of k+1 pairwise-distinct vertices v_0, v_1, ..., v_k with v_{i-1} -> v_i for every 1 <= i <= k; the length is the number of arcs k, not the number of vertices. Proposition: every finite oriented graph D with delta+(D) >= 4 contains a directed path of length 8.

rows.title: Delta = 4, n = 12 frontier case (first genuinely open size)
rows.statement_text: Let D = (V, A) be a finite oriented graph (a digraph with no 2-cycle: for no distinct u, v are both u -> v and v -> u arcs). d+(v) is the number of arcs with tail v and delta+(D) := min_v d+(v). A directed path of length k is a sequence of k+1 pairwise-distinct vertices v_0, ..., v_k with v_{i-1} -> v_i for 1 <= i <= k (length = number of arcs). Proposition: every oriented graph D with delta+(D) >= 4 and |V(D)| = 12 contains a directed path of length 8.

rows.title: Jackson 1981 minimum-semidegree theorem (transcription unverified; standing working hypothesis)
rows.statement_text: Let D be a finite oriented graph (no 2-cycles) and k >= 1 an integer. Let d+(v), d-(v) be the numbers of arcs with tail v and head v respectively, delta+(D) := min_v d+(v), delta-(D) := min_v d-(v), and delta0(D) := min(delta+(D), delta-(D)) the minimum semidegree. A directed Hamilton cycle is a directed cycle passing through every vertex of D exactly once; a directed path of length 2k is a sequence of 2k+1 pairwise-distinct vertices each sending an arc to the next. Proposition (Jackson 1981): if delta0(D) >= k, then (i) D contains a directed Hamilton cycle when |V(D)| <= 2k+2, and (ii) D contains a directed path of length 2k when |V(D)| > 2k+2.

rows.title: '+1 strengthening' of Cheng-Keevash Lemma 7
rows.statement_text: Let delta >= 1 be an integer and D a finite oriented graph (no 2-cycles) with delta+(D) >= delta, where delta+(D) := min_v d+(v) and d+(v) is the number of arcs with tail v. Let l(D) denote the maximum number of arcs in a directed simple path of D (a sequence of pairwise-distinct vertices each sending an arc to the next). For an induced subgraph S of D (the sub-digraph on a vertex subset with all arcs of D between its vertices), delta+(S) := min_{v in V(S)} |{w in V(S) : v -> w}|. Proposition: either D contains a directed path of length 2*delta, or D has an induced subgraph S with |V(S)| <= delta and delta+(S) >= 2*delta + 1 - l(D).

rows.title: Thomasse girth strengthening (refuted for g >= 4 by explicit D_{a,b} counterexamples)
rows.statement_text: Let D be a finite digraph with delta+(D) >= delta (delta+(D) := min_v d+(v), d+(v) the number of arcs with tail v) and girth g, where the girth is the minimum number of arcs in a directed cycle of D. Thomasse's girth strengthening asserts: D contains a directed simple path of length delta*(g-1) (a sequence of delta*(g-1)+1 pairwise-distinct vertices each sending an arc to the next). DISPROVED for every g >= 4 (with delta >= 2): define the k-lift of a vertex v as deleting all arcs with tail v, adding k-1 pairwise-disjoint sets U_{v,1}, ..., U_{v,k-1} of delta new vertices each, setting U_{v,0} := {v} and U_{v,k} := N+(v), and adding all arcs from U_{v,i-1} to U_{v,i} for 1 <= i <= k (a 1-lift does nothing; every lift preserves all out-degrees = delta). Let D_{a,b} be the complete digraph on delta+1 vertices with one vertex a-lifted and every other vertex b-lifted. Then (Claim 6) D_{a,b} has girth a+b and longest directed path of length exactly delta*b + a - 1. Taking a = b = g/2 for even g, or a = (g-1)/2 and b = (g+1)/2 for odd g, yields for every g >= 4 and delta >= 2 a digraph of girth g with delta+ = delta whose longest path is shorter than delta*(g-1). Smallest instance: g = 4, delta = 2 gives D_{2,2} on 9 vertices with longest path 5 < 6 = delta*(g-1).

rows.title: Theorem A (single-tool): no biplanar 10-chromatic odd-cycle clique blowup with n ≤ 30, ω ≤ 8
rows.statement_text: For all integers r ≥ 1 and a_1, …, a_{2r+1} ≥ 1, let G := C_{2r+1}[K_{a_1}, …, K_{a_{2r+1}}] be the weighted odd-cycle clique blowup: V(G) = F_1 ⊔ … ⊔ F_{2r+1} with |F_i| = a_i ('fibres'), and distinct x ∈ F_i, y ∈ F_j adjacent iff i = j or i − j ≡ ±1 (mod 2r+1). If n := Σ_i a_i ≤ 30, the clique number ω(G) ≤ 8 (for r ≥ 2 this equals max_i (a_i + a_{i+1 mod 2r+1}); it implies G is K_9-free), χ(G) ≥ 10 (no proper 9-coloring), and |E(G)| ≤ 6n − 12, then G is not biplanar, i.e., E(G) admits no partition into two sets each forming a planar graph on V(G).

rows.title: Sub-bracket chi_EM >= 10 (refute folklore chi_EM = 9)
rows.statement_text: There exists a finite simple graph G = (V, E) that is biplanar — i.e., E admits a partition E = E1 ⊔ E2 such that both (V, E1) and (V, E2) are planar (embeddable in the plane with no edge crossings; equivalently containing neither K_5 nor K_{3,3} as a minor) — and that admits no proper vertex coloring with 9 colors, i.e., there is no map c : V → {1,…,9} with c(u) ≠ c(v) for every uv ∈ E. Equivalently, chi_EM := max{ χ(G) : G biplanar } ≥ 10, where χ(G) is the least k admitting a proper k-coloring.

rows.title: Target density lemma: 12-critical K_9-free graphs have at least 6n − 11 edges
rows.statement_text: For every finite simple graph G on n = |V(G)| vertices such that (i) G is 12-critical — χ(G) = 12 (G has a proper 12-coloring but no proper 11-coloring) and every proper subgraph H ⊊ G satisfies χ(H) ≤ 11 — and (ii) G contains no K_9, i.e., no set of 9 pairwise-adjacent vertices, the edge count satisfies |E(G)| ≥ 6n − 11 (equivalently |E(G)| > 6n − 12).

rows.title: Fork C capacity claim: every 35-edge high-only K_7-chunk profile is non-biplanar (REFUTED)
rows.statement_text: REFUTED CLAIM: every finite simple graph G with V(G) = C ⊔ A such that G[C] ≅ K_7, A is an independent set in G, every edge incident to a vertex of A has its other endpoint in C, and the number of C–A edges equals 35, fails to be biplanar (its edge set admits no partition into two planar subgraphs on V(G)). COUNTEREXAMPLE (explicit in docs/phase6_discharge_attempt.md §7.16): C = {c_0,…,c_6} inducing K_7, A = {a_0,…,a_6}, with a_i adjacent to exactly the five vertices c_j, j ∉ {i, i+1 (mod 7)} (each outside vertex misses one consecutive cyclic pair); n = 14, m = C(7,2) + 7·5 = 56; this balanced cyclic profile was reported biplanar (SMS SAT, 0.011 s).

rows.title: Q0 closure: no self-reproducing contraction scenario at n = 89
rows.statement_text: There is no pair (G, v) such that: (i) G is a finite simple graph that is 12-critical (χ(G) = 12, every proper subgraph 11-colorable), contains no K_9 (no 9 pairwise-adjacent vertices), and is biplanar (E(G) partitions into two planar subgraphs on V(G)), with |V(G)| = 89 and |E(G)| = 522 = 6·89 − 12; (ii) v ∈ V(G) has deg_G(v) = 11 and every neighbor of v has degree ≥ 12; (iii) the induced subgraph G[N(v)] is a vertex-disjoint union of complete graphs (necessarily each of order ≤ 7, since adding v would otherwise create a K_9); and (iv) for every pair of non-adjacent vertices u, u' ∈ N(v) lying in distinct components (cliques) of G[N(v)], the simple graph G* obtained from G − v by identifying u with u' (merging parallel edges) is itself a 12-critical K_9-free graph on 87 vertices with exactly 511 edges (the edge count 511 = 522 − 11 − q forces q = 0, i.e., u and u' have no common neighbor in G − v).

rows.title: Step 4+: some q ≥ 1 non-edge in N(v) contracts K_9-safely
rows.statement_text: Let G be any finite simple graph that is 12-critical (χ(G) = 12 and every proper subgraph is 11-colorable), K_9-free (no 9 pairwise-adjacent vertices), and biplanar (E(G) partitions into two planar subgraphs on V(G)). Let L := {x ∈ V(G) : deg_G(x) = 11} and suppose v ∈ L is isolated in the induced subgraph G[L], i.e., no neighbor of v has degree 11 (so |N(v)| = 11 and N(v) contains at least 6 non-adjacent pairs). For distinct non-adjacent u, u' ∈ N(v), set q(u,u') := |N_{G−v}(u) ∩ N_{G−v}(u')| (number of common neighbors in G − v), and call the non-edge {u,u'} K_9-safe if the simple graph obtained from G − v by identifying u with u' (replacing parallel edges by single edges) contains no K_9. CLAIM: if at least one non-edge {u,u'} ⊆ N(v) has q(u,u') ≥ 1, then at least one non-edge {u,u'} ⊆ N(v) with q(u,u') ≥ 1 is K_9-safe (equivalently, admits no 'split obstruction': no K_8 in G − v inside N(u) ∪ N(u') meeting both N(u)∖N(u') and N(u')∖N(u)).
