rows.title: G1 — refuted: every in-class digraph has maximum out-degree <= 1 (functional-digraph lemma)
rows.statement_text: REFUTED CLAIM: every finite digraph in Forb_ind({digon, ->C3, S2+}) (definitions as in row H1) has maximum out-degree at most 1, i.e. is a functional digraph. EXPLICIT COUNTEREXAMPLE: the transitive tournament TT3 on vertices {0,1,2} with arcs 0->1, 0->2, 1->2 is in the class (oriented; no directed triangle; every out-neighbourhood induces a tournament, so no induced S2+) and vertex 0 has out-degree 2. More generally TT_k is in-class with out-degree k-1 (TT4 gives out-degree 3). Root cause: the class forbids only the DIRECTED triangle, not the transitive triangle, so out-neighbourhoods can be transitive tournaments of any size.

rows.title: G11 — refuted: min-FAS nesting lemma (some minimum feedback-arc-set order has a cut crossed by <= 1 back-arc)
rows.statement_text: REFUTED CLAIM: for every finite digraph D in Forb_ind({digon, ->C3, S2+}) (definitions as in row H1) on n vertices, there exist a linear order pi of V(D) minimizing the number of back-arcs (arcs u->v with pi(v) < pi(u); i.e. a minimum feedback-arc-set order) and a cut position c in {1,...,n-1} such that at most one back-arc crosses the cut (i.e. at most one back-arc u->v has pi(v) <= c < pi(u)) — 'crossing-width <= 1 at some cut'. EXPLICIT COUNTEREXAMPLE: C7(2,4), the circulant on Z_7 with arcs i->i+2 and i->i+4 (mod 7), arc list [[0,2],[3,0],[0,4],[5,0],[1,3],[4,1],[1,5],[6,1],[2,4],[5,2],[2,6],[3,5],[6,3],[4,6]] (as recorded in the ledger): it is in-class, vertex-transitive, chi_d = 2, has minimum back-arc count 3, and over ALL minimum-FAS orders every cut is crossed by at least 2 back-arcs; the best achievable min-over-cuts crossing-width is 2 (e.g. the order (0,2,4,6,1,3,5) has per-cut widths [2,3,3,3,3,2]).

rows.title: G12 — refuted: parity/alternate-interval 2-colouring of round in-class members
rows.statement_text: REFUTED CLAIM: for every ROUND member D of Forb_ind({digon, ->C3, S2+}) (round as defined in row H7, with round cyclic labelling v_0,...,v_{n-1}), the parity-along-round-order 2-colouring — v_i coloured i mod 2, i.e. the partition into even-indexed and odd-indexed vertices — is an acyclic 2-partition (each colour class induces a subdigraph with no directed cycle). EXPLICIT COUNTEREXAMPLE: C10(1,2,3) (arcs i->i+1, i->i+2, i->i+3 mod 10) is in-class and round in its natural cyclic labelling, but the even class {0,2,4,6,8} induces the directed 5-cycle 0->2->4->6->8->0 via the jump-2 arcs (and likewise the odd class), so the parity partition is not acyclic. The ledger records the parity rule invalid for C_n(1,2,3) for every n = 10..15, whereas a single contiguous interval of size 3 does give a valid 2-dicolouring of C10(1,2,3) (50 valid interval-partitions).

rows.title: G8 — refuted: every nontrivial strong component of an in-class member has a vertex of in-degree <= 2
rows.statement_text: REFUTED CLAIM: for every finite digraph D in Forb_ind({digon, ->C3, S2+}) (definitions as in row H1), every strongly connected induced subdigraph with at least 2 vertices (every nontrivial strong component) contains a vertex whose in-degree within that subdigraph is at most 2 (and symmetrically a vertex of out-degree at most 2), so that strong components are 2-in-degenerate and peelable. EXPLICIT COUNTEREXAMPLE: C10(1,2,3), the circulant digraph on Z_10 with arcs i->i+1, i->i+2, i->i+3 (mod 10), is in the class (oriented, no directed triangle, every N+(x) = {x+1,x+2,x+3} induces a transitive tournament), is a single strong component on all 10 vertices, and is 3-in-regular AND 3-out-regular (minimum in-degree = minimum out-degree = 3 everywhere), with girth 4 and chi_d = 2. No vertex of in-degree <= 2 exists, so no degeneracy/peeling order exists.

rows.title: Conjecture 6.2 — chi_d(Forb_ind(digon, ->C3, S2+)) = 2
rows.statement_text: Every finite loopless digraph D that (a) contains no digon (no pair of vertices u != v with both arcs u->v and v->u; equivalently D is an oriented graph), (b) contains no directed triangle ->C3 (no vertices a,b,c with a->b, b->c, c->a; in an oriented graph a directed triangle is automatically induced), and (c) contains no induced out-star S2+ (no three distinct vertices x,a,b with x->a and x->b such that there is no arc between a and b in either direction and no arc a->x or b->x; in an oriented graph this is equivalent to: some vertex x has two out-neighbours joined by no arc, i.e. some out-neighbourhood N+(x) does not induce a tournament) satisfies chi_d(D) <= 2, where the dichromatic number chi_d(D) is the least k such that V(D) can be partitioned into k sets each inducing a subdigraph with no directed cycle. Since the directed 4-cycle belongs to the class and has chi_d = 2, this is equivalent to chi_d(Forb_ind({digon, ->C3, S2+})) = 2 exactly.

rows.title: Class identity — Forb_ind(digon, ->C3, S2+) = oriented ->C3-free out-local-tournaments with transitive out-neighbourhoods
rows.statement_text: For every finite loopless digraph D the following are equivalent: (1) D contains no induced digon, no induced directed triangle ->C3, and no induced out-star S2+ (definitions as in row H1); (2) D is an oriented graph with no directed 3-cycle such that for every vertex x the out-neighbourhood N+(x) = {y : x->y} induces a tournament (every two out-neighbours are joined by exactly one arc), i.e. D is an out-local-tournament. Moreover, in any D satisfying (2), every N+(x) induces a TRANSITIVE tournament (a tournament whose arc relation is transitive; equivalently, a tournament with no directed triangle), since a directed triangle inside N+(x) would be a directed triangle of D.

rows.title: HALF A — contiguous interval of length d and its complement 2-dicolour the circulant C_n<1..d>
rows.statement_text: For all integers d >= 1 and n >= 2d+1, let C_n<1..d> denote the circulant digraph with vertex set Z_n and arc set {i -> (i+j) mod n : i in Z_n, j in {1,...,d}}. Then for every a in Z_n the contiguous interval I_a = {a, a+1, ..., a+d-1} (residues mod n) and its complement Z_n \ I_a each induce an acyclic subdigraph of C_n<1..d> (no directed cycle); hence the partition {I_a, Z_n \ I_a} witnesses chi_d(C_n<1..d>) <= 2 uniformly in n. (By rotation-invariance of circulants the choice of a is immaterial.) This is 'HALF A' of ledger entry H6: the closed-form acyclic 2-partition of the dense round in-class circulants — the residual hard family of Conjecture 6.2, concrete model C10(1,2,3) = C_10<1..3> — covering in particular every C_n<1..d> that lies in Forb_ind({digon, ->C3, S2+}) (the ->C3-free ones, d roughly <= n/3).

rows.title: Localization identity — non-round = non-locally-in-semicomplete = embedded in-star, for strong in-class members
rows.statement_text: For every strongly connected finite digraph D in Forb_ind({digon, ->C3, S2+}) (definitions as in row H1) the following are equivalent: (1) D is NOT round, where a digraph D on vertices labelled v_0,...,v_{n-1} is ROUND if there is a cyclic labelling such that for every i, N+(v_i) = {v_{i+1}, ..., v_{i+d+(v_i)}} and N-(v_i) = {v_{i-d-(v_i)}, ..., v_{i-1}} with indices mod n and d+(v_i), d-(v_i) the out- and in-degrees (each out-neighbourhood is a segment of consecutive vertices immediately following v_i, each in-neighbourhood a segment immediately preceding v_i); (2) D is NOT locally in-semicomplete: some in-neighbourhood N-(v) = {u : u->v} does not induce a tournament; (3) D has a vertex v whose in-neighbourhood contains an independent pair — two vertices a, b with a->v and b->v and no arc between a and b in either direction (an embedded in-star S2-, where S2- is the 3-vertex digraph {1,2}->0). ((2)<=>(3) is definitional in an oriented graph; the substantive content is (1)<=>(2): the round strong in-class members are exactly the locally-in-semicomplete ones.)

rows.title: Cyclic substitution preserves induced-P+(2)-freeness for all cycle lengths (refuted: directed C4)
rows.statement_text: For every integer k >= 3 and all finite digraphs D_1, ..., D_k each containing no induced copy of P+(2) (the directed path on 3 vertices {0,1,2} with arcs (0,1),(1,2) and 0, 2 non-adjacent), the cyclic substitution C_k(D_1,...,D_k) — disjoint copies of D_1, ..., D_k plus, for each i, all arcs from every vertex of copy i to every vertex of copy (i+1 mod k) — contains no induced copy of P+(2). (This 'general bundle mechanism' was proposed to explain why the tournament tower avoids induced P+(2) in any C_k-substitution.)

rows.title: C4-substitution tower stays triangle-free / in Forb_ind(K2,K3,P+(3)) (refuted: T_3 contains TT3)
rows.statement_text: Every member of the C4-substitution tower defined by T_1 = K1 (one vertex) and T_{i+1} = C_4(T_i, T_i, T_i, T_i) — substitution into the directed 4-cycle: four disjoint copies of T_i plus all arcs from every vertex of copy j to every vertex of copy (j+1 mod 4), for j = 0,1,2,3 — is triangle-free, i.e., contains no induced orientation of K3 (no three pairwise adjacent vertices; forbids both TT3, the transitive 3-vertex tournament, and the directed 3-cycle C3); hence every T_i, being also digon-free and free of induced P+(3) (directed path on 4 vertices, arcs (0,1),(1,2),(2,3), no other adjacencies) with chi_d(T_i) = i, lies in Forb_ind(K2, K3, P+(3)) and witnesses that {K2, K3, P+(3)} is not heroic (a disproof of H1 at k = 3).

rows.title: Long chordless directed cycles avoid induced P+(4) (refuted: C6 contains P+(4))
rows.statement_text: For every integer m >= 6, the directed cycle on m vertices — vertex set {0,...,m-1}, arc set {(i, (i+1) mod m)}, no other arcs — contains no induced copy of P+(4), the directed path on 5 vertices {0,...,4} with arc set {(0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,4)} and no other adjacencies (induced containment: an injection f such that for all ordered pairs of distinct x, y, (x,y) is an arc of P+(4) iff (f(x),f(y)) is an arc of the host). (This was the load-bearing step of the G6 reduction: it would imply the Harutyunyan-Mohar high-digirth triangle-free digon-free family with unbounded chi_d avoids induced P+(4), hence lies in Forb_ind(K2, K3, P+(4)), disproving H1 at k = 4 and making P+(3) vs P+(4) the exact heroic boundary.)

rows.title: {K2, K3, P+(k)} is heroic for every k (sufficiency instance of Conjecture 4.2)
rows.statement_text: For every integer k >= 1 there exists a constant c(k) such that every finite digraph D satisfying (i) D has no digon (no distinct vertices u, v with both arcs (u,v) and (v,u); i.e., D is an oriented graph, equivalently no induced K2sym), (ii) D is triangle-free: no three distinct vertices are pairwise adjacent, where u, v are adjacent iff at least one of (u,v), (v,u) is an arc — equivalently D contains no induced copy of any orientation of K3, i.e., neither TT3 (the transitive tournament on 3 vertices, arcs (0,1),(0,2),(1,2)) nor the directed 3-cycle C3, and (iii) D contains no induced copy of P+(k), the directed path on k+1 vertices {0,...,k} with arc set {(i,i+1) : 0 <= i < k} and no other adjacencies (induced containment: an injection f with (x,y) an arc of P+(k) iff (f(x),f(y)) an arc of D, for all ordered pairs of distinct vertices), has dichromatic number chi_d(D) <= c(k), where chi_d(D) is the least r such that V(D) partitions into r classes each inducing a subdigraph with no directed cycle. Equivalently: the set {K2, K3, P+(k)} is heroic for every fixed k.

rows.title: {K2, P+(m)} is non-heroic for every m >= 2 (tournament tower)
rows.statement_text: For every integer m >= 2, the class Forb_ind(K2, P+(m)) — all finite digraphs with no digon (no distinct u, v carrying both arcs (u,v) and (v,u)) and no induced copy of P+(m), the directed path on m+1 vertices {0,...,m} with arcs {(i,i+1) : 0 <= i < m} and no other adjacencies — has unbounded dichromatic number chi_d (least number of classes in a vertex partition each inducing a directed-cycle-free subdigraph); i.e., {K2, P+(m)} is not heroic. Witness family: the tournament tower T_1 = K1 (one vertex, no arcs), T_j = C3(T_{j-1}, T_{j-1}, K1), where C3(A,B,C) is substitution into the directed 3-cycle: disjoint copies of A, B, C plus all arcs from every vertex of A to every vertex of B, from B to C, and from C to A. Each T_j is a tournament (every pair of vertices adjacent, no digon), hence contains no induced P+(m) for any m >= 2 (P+(m) has a non-adjacent pair), and chi_d(T_j) = j for every j >= 1.

rows.title: Triangle-free + digon-free digraphs with chi_d >= 3 exist ({K2, K3} not heroic with bound 2)
rows.statement_text: There exists a finite digraph D that is digon-free (no distinct vertices u, v with both arcs (u,v) and (v,u)) and triangle-free (no three distinct vertices pairwise adjacent, where adjacency means at least one arc between the pair; equivalently no induced orientation of K3, i.e., no TT3 and no directed 3-cycle) with dichromatic number chi_d(D) >= 3, where chi_d(D) is the least r such that V(D) partitions into r classes each inducing a subdigraph with no directed cycle. Equivalently: the set {K2, K3} is not heroic with bound 2. Any witness has at least 9 vertices: all orientations of all triangle-free graphs on n <= 8 vertices have chi_d <= 2 (exhaustive), and all 2^19 orientations of the Groetzsch graph (n = 11) have chi_d <= 2 (two independent exhaustive methods).

rows.title: Bridgeless counter-examples to ell(G)+br(G) >= |G| are finite
rows.statement_text: There exists N in NAT such that for every finite connected simple bridgeless graph G with n = |V(G)| >= N, ell(G) >= n. Equivalently (since there are only finitely many graphs of each order up to isomorphism): up to isomorphism there are only finitely many connected bridgeless graphs G with ell(G) + br(G) < |V(G)| (for bridgeless G this reads ell(G) < |V(G)|). Definitions: G is bridgeless iff it has no bridge, i.e. no edge e with G - e disconnected (so br(G) = 0); d(u,v) is the shortest-path (hop) distance in G; [p q r] holds iff d(p,q) + d(q,r) = d(p,r); for distinct vertices a,b, line(a,b) = {a,b} UNION {x in V(G) \ {a,b} : [a b x] or [a x b] or [x a b]}; ell(G) is the number of distinct sets line(a,b) over all unordered pairs {a,b} of distinct vertices.

rows.title: Additive substitution upper bound omega_vec(S[H]) <= omega_vec(S)+omega_vec(H)-1
rows.statement_text: For all tournaments S and H, omega_vec(S[H]) <= omega_vec(S) + omega_vec(H) - 1, where S[H] is the lexicographic substitution (V(S[H]) = V(S) x V(H); arc (u,x)->(v,y) iff u->v in S, or u=v and x->y in H) and omega_vec(T) is the tournament clique number: the minimum over all total orders prec of V(T) of the clique number of the backedge graph T^prec (edge {u,v}, u prec v, iff the arc of T is v->u).

rows.title: Dic-gap barrier: the dichromatic-clique gap reopens under every C3 lift
rows.statement_text: For every tournament H with dic(H) = omega_vec(H), it holds that dic(C3[H]) > omega_vec(C3[H]). Here omega_vec(T) is the tournament clique number: the minimum over all total orders prec of V(T) of the clique number omega(T^prec) of the backedge graph T^prec, which has an edge {u,v} with u prec v iff the arc of T is v->u; dic(T) is the dichromatic number: the minimum number of parts in a partition of V(T) into sets each inducing an acyclic subdigraph; and C3[H] is the lexicographic substitution of H into the directed 3-cycle: three disjoint copies H_0,H_1,H_2 of H with every arc from H_i to H_{i+1 mod 3} between copies and the arcs of H inside copies. Consequence if true: the Aubian-Coulomb Prop 6.2 lift (if dic(H)=omega_vec(H)=k and dic(H-v)=k-1 for all v, then C3[H] is (k+1)-omega_vec-critical) can fire at most once per supply object and cannot be iterated.

rows.title: Pod-tightness of the iterated-triangle layer-product growth: lambda = 3/2
rows.statement_text: Let B_0 = TT_1 (a single vertex) and B_k = C3[B_{k-1}] (lexicographic substitution into the directed 3-cycle), so V(B_k) = {0,1,2}^k with arc x->y iff y_j = x_j + 1 (mod 3), where j is the first coordinate at which x and y differ; colour that arc c = x_j. For each c in {0,1,2} the colour-c arcs form a transitive partial order P_c. For a total order pi of V(B_k), let q_c(pi) be the maximum length r of a P_c-chain v_1 <_{P_c} ... <_{P_c} v_r that is pi-decreasing (v_r pi-before ... pi-before v_1), and set L_k = min over total orders pi of q_0(pi)*q_1(pi)*q_2(pi). The limit lambda = lim_{k->infty} L_k^{1/k} exists (L_k is submultiplicative) and satisfies 3/2 <= lambda <= 24^{1/5}. Conjecture (pod-tight side): lambda = 3/2, i.e. L_k = (3/2)^{k+o(k)}.

rows.title: Pack-coupled D25-ring reaches chi_vec >= 4 (n <= 175) — disproved, all 12 instances 3-dicolourable
rows.statement_text: There exist L in {3,5,7}, a pack offset d in {1,2}, and one of the two coded interface orientations such that the pack-coupled D25-ring — L disjoint copies of D25 = C5<-5 (defined as: vertices u_{p,j}, p in Z_5, j in {0..4}, arcs u_{p,j}->u_{p+1,j'} for j != j' and u_{p+1,j}->u_{p,j}) placed on a directed L-cycle, with, for each k in Z_L, a complete bipartite set of like-oriented arcs between one 5-vertex independent pack of copy k and the pack at position offset d of copy k+1 (exact parametrization: scripts/constructions.py:pack_coupled_d25_ring) — is an oriented triangle-free digraph with dichromatic number chi_vec >= 4 (giving m(4) <= 25L <= 175).

rows.title: Degree floor d+(v)*d-(v) >= 10 for 3-dichromatic digon-free digraphs — disproved by Paley P7
rows.statement_text: Every digon-free digraph D (no loops, no pair of opposite arcs) with dichromatic number chi_vec(D) >= 3 — chi_vec(D) is the least k such that V(D) partitions into k sets each inducing a subdigraph with no directed cycle — contains a vertex v with d+(v)*d-(v) >= 10 (out-degree times in-degree); equivalently max_v sqrt(d+(v)d-(v)) >= 3/(1-e^-13) = 3.0000068.

rows.title: Grötzsch t-backward-blowup below t = 19 reaches chi_vec >= 4 (searched orientation grid) — disproved on every resolved instance
rows.statement_text: At least one of the following digraphs has dichromatic number chi_vec >= 4: the t-backward-blowup of an orientation Dor of the Grötzsch graph (the Mycielskian of C5: 11 vertices, 20 edges, triangle-free, chromatic number 4, independence number 5), where the t-backward-blowup replaces each vertex x by an independent pack of t columns x_0..x_{t-1} and each arc x->y by forward arcs x_j->y_{j'} for all j != j' plus matched backward arcs y_j->x_j (always oriented and triangle-free), ranging over the resolved search grid: all 32 searched orientations (the acyclic one, 30 random, balanced/Eulerian non-acyclic) for t in {2..10}; the acyclic, balanced-non-acyclic and random orientations for t in {11..15}; the acyclic and three random orientations for t = 16; the acyclic (lo-hi) orientation for t = 17; and the acyclic orientation for t = 18 (n = 11t <= 198). rows.title: Pent5(D25) is 4-dichromatic (would give m(4) <= 125) — disproved, chi_vec = 3
rows.statement_text: The digraph Pent5(D25) — 5 disjoint copies of D25 indexed by i in Z_5, where D25 = C5<-5 is the oriented triangle-free digraph on vertices u_{p,j} (p in Z_5 = pack/cycle position, j in {0..4} = column) with arcs u_{p,j}->u_{p+1,j'} for all j != j' and u_{p+1,j}->u_{p,j}; all internal D25 arcs kept, plus for each copy i, each pack p, and each column j the interface arc (i,p,j) -> (i+1 mod 5, p, j+1 mod 5) (n = 125, 750 arcs; oracle-verified oriented and triangle-free) — has dichromatic number chi_vec >= 4; this would give m(4) <= 125, where m(k) is the least order of an oriented triangle-free digraph with chi_vec >= k (paper benchmark: m(4) <= 209).

rows.title: Process-graph orientation route: a_vec(n) = O(sqrt(n log n)) via the triangle-free process
rows.statement_text: There is a constant C > 0 such that, with probability tending to 1 as n -> infinity, the graph G_n produced by the triangle-free random graph process on n vertices (start from the empty graph on [n]; repeatedly add an edge chosen uniformly at random among the non-edges whose addition creates no triangle, until the graph is maximally triangle-free; Bohman-Keevash) admits an orientation D (each edge {u,v} receives exactly one of the arcs u->v, v->u, so D is an oriented graph: a digraph with no loops and no pair of opposite arcs) in which every acyclic set has size at most C*sqrt(n*log n), where an acyclic set of D is a set S of vertices such that the induced subdigraph D[S] contains no directed cycle. This implies the open upper half of the paper's Conjecture 3: a_vec(n) = O(sqrt(n log n)), where a_vec(n) is the minimum over all n-vertex triangle-free oriented graphs D of alpha_vec(D) = the maximum size of an acyclic set of D.

rows.title: FPY 2024 bound pi(L_fpy box L_fpy, r) <= 96 for all roots — published but locally uncertified (the folder's blocked reproduction gate)
rows.statement_text: Let L_fpy be the simple graph on vertex set {0,...,7} with the 13 edges {0-1, 0-2, 1-3, 2-4, 2-5, 2-6, 3-4, 3-5, 3-6, 3-7, 4-7, 5-7, 6-7}, and let L_fpy box L_fpy be the Cartesian product (vertex set V(L_fpy) x V(L_fpy); (u,v) ~ (u',v') iff (u = u' and vv' in E(L_fpy)) or (v = v' and uu' in E(L_fpy))). A configuration is C : V -> Z_{>=0} with size |C| = sum_v C(v); a pebbling move removes 2 pebbles from a vertex u with C(u) >= 2 and adds 1 pebble to a neighbour of u; C is r-solvable iff some finite sequence of pebbling moves yields at least one pebble on r. The rooted pebbling number pi(G, r) is the least t such that every configuration of size t on G is r-solvable, and pi(G) = max_{r in V(G)} pi(G, r). PROPOSITION: for every root r = (r1, r2) in V(L_fpy) x V(L_fpy), pi(L_fpy box L_fpy, r) <= 96; equivalently pi(L_fpy box L_fpy) <= 96.

rows.title: Lemke-square instance of Graham's pebbling conjecture: pi(L_fpy box L_fpy) <= 64 (class-0 dichotomy)
rows.statement_text: Let L_fpy be the simple graph on vertex set {0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7} with the 13 edges {0-1, 0-2, 1-3, 2-4, 2-5, 2-6, 3-4, 3-5, 3-6, 3-7, 4-7, 5-7, 6-7} (the 8-vertex Lemke graph in the Flocco-Pulaj-Yerger labelling; degree sequence (5,4,4,3,3,3,2,2)). Let L_fpy box L_fpy denote the Cartesian product: vertex set V(L_fpy) x V(L_fpy), with (u,v) adjacent to (u',v') iff either (u = u' and vv' in E(L_fpy)) or (v = v' and uu' in E(L_fpy)). A configuration on a graph G is a function C : V(G) -> Z_{>=0}; its size is |C| = sum_v C(v). A pebbling move from C removes 2 pebbles from a vertex u with C(u) >= 2 and adds 1 pebble to a neighbour v of u. C is r-solvable iff some finite sequence of pebbling moves starting from C produces a configuration with at least one pebble on the root r; otherwise C is r-unsolvable. The pebbling number pi(G) is the least t such that for every r in V(G), every configuration of size t on G is r-solvable. CONJECTURE: pi(L_fpy box L_fpy) <= 64. Equivalently (since pi(G) >= |V(G)| for every graph G: place one pebble on each vertex other than r, then no move is possible), pi(L_fpy box L_fpy) = 64, i.e. L_fpy box L_fpy is class 0. Equivalently: for every r in V(L_fpy) x V(L_fpy), every configuration of size 64 on L_fpy box L_fpy is r-solvable. A refutation would be an explicit finite certificate: a root r and a 64-pebble r-unsolvable configuration.

rows.title: Naive active-bag DP signature is extension-complete (refuted)
rows.statement_text: Let T be a tournament with radius-2 score windows I_v = [max(0, d^-(v)-2), min(n-1, d^-(v)+2)] (d^-(v) = indegree), satisfying Hall feasibility (for every position interval [l,r], #{v : I_v subseteq [l,r]} <= r-l+1); every LFO places each v at a position in I_v (proved score-window lemma). For a valid prefix (an initial segment of an order extendable in principle to an LFO, with forced back-arcs preloaded by the forced/flexible solver) at cut p, define the ACTIVE-BAG SIGNATURE as: the set of active vertices (v with p in I_v), the placed subset of the active bag, the loaded back-arc degrees of the active vertices, and the component partition of the loaded back-arc graph restricted to the active bag. CLAIM (refuted): any two valid same-length prefixes of the same T with identical active-bag signature have the same extendability - both extend to a complete LFO or neither does.

rows.title: Strong AC-completeness of the apex-cut CSP (refuted by witness 8#1079)
rows.statement_text: Let T be a tournament. For each vertex v define the apex-cut graph C_v: an edge ab for each directed triangle v->a->b->v (a in N+(v), b in N-(v), a->b). Domain D_v = { P subseteq V\{v} : |P| <= 2 and C_v - P is a linear forest } (P = candidate set of F-neighbours of v, since a Path-FAS witness F must be a linear forest, giving |N_F(v)| <= 2; the proved apex-cut lemma says F hits every directed triangle iff E(C_v - P_v) subseteq F for all v). Run arc-consistency (AC-3) on the binary constraints (symmetry: u in P_v iff v in P_u; forced edges: xy in E(C_v - P_v) implies y in P_x and x in P_y). Let the mandatory-forced graph M be the set of edges forced into F by every AC-surviving candidate of some vertex. CLAIM (refuted): if after AC every domain D_v is nonempty and M is acyclic as an undirected graph, then T is Path-FAS YES, i.e. some order of T has a linear-forest back-arc graph.

Run arc-consistency (AC-3) on the binary constraints (symmetry: u in P_v iff v in P_u; forced edges: xy in E(C_v - P_v) implies y in P_x and x in P_y). Let the mandatory-forced graph M be the set of edges forced into F by every AC-surviving candidate of some vertex. CLAIM (refuted): if after AC every domain D_v is nonempty and M is acyclic as an undirected graph, then T is Path-FAS YES, i.e. some order of T has a linear-forest back-arc graph.

rows.title: Dormant-Matching Quotient Lemma (multiset aggregate) (refuted)
rows.statement_text: Setting of row visible-latent. Let H be the forced-backedge digraph of T (arcs u->v of T whose score windows are disjoint with I_v strictly below I_u, so every candidate LFO places v before u and u->v is a back-arc; H-edges are preloaded). At cut p, a DORMANT H-COMPONENT is a connected component C of the underlying undirected graph of H with C disjoint from the active band A_p and containing at least one closed (window ended, placed) and one future (window not yet open) vertex. Its LOCAL PROFILE is (canonical shape of C = sorted tuple of H-degrees; sorted list over v in C of (status(v) in {closed, future}, loaded back-arc degree of v, sorted set of active-band position indices that v can hit via a flexible back-arc)). The DORMANT AGGREGATE of a prefix is the multiset of local profiles of its dormant H-components. CLAIM (refuted): any two valid length-p prefixes of the same T with the same visible-latent signature and equal dormant aggregates have the same extendability to a complete LFO.

rows.title: Capacity-form Lemma C (Fanout Barrier): no EQ_2 gadget has joint capacity on both equality values
rows.statement_text: Let T be a tournament (an orientation of the complete graph) on vertex set V, n = |V|. For a linear order sigma of V, an arc u->v of T is a back-arc of sigma iff sigma places v before u; the back-arc graph B_sigma is the undirected graph on V with an edge {u,v} for every back-arc u->v. A linear forest is an undirected graph with maximum degree <= 2 and no cycle. sigma is an LFO iff B_sigma is a linear forest. A port is an ordered pair (x,y) of distinct vertices; its raw bit under sigma is b = 1 iff y precedes x in sigma. Fix two vertex-disjoint ports P1 = (x1,y1), P2 = (x2,y2) (the four endpoints pairwise distinct) and an orientation o = (o1,o2) in {0,1}^2; the realized relation is R = { (b1(sigma) XOR o1, b2(sigma) XOR o2) : sigma an LFO of T }. The gadget is EQ_2 iff R = {(0,0),(1,1)}. A vector (c1,c2) has JOINT CAPACITY iff some LFO sigma realizing it has all four port endpoints x1,y1,x2,y2 of B_sigma-degree <= 1. CONJECTURE: for every n, every tournament T, every vertex-disjoint port pair and orientation with R = EQ_2, joint capacity does NOT hold on both (0,0) and (1,1). Equivalently (via the in-folder proved theorem cap-11 = iso-11): no EQ_2 gadget is simultaneously cap-00 and iso-11.

rows.title: Joint-invariant ansatz condition (a): I(v*) >= T at the max-degsum ear
rows.statement_text: Let G be a 2-tree on n >= 4 vertices, v a simplicial degree-2 ear with supporting edge {a,b}, H := G - v, and w := e_a + e_b in R^{n-1} (so ||w||^2 = 2). Let P- be the spectral projector of A(H) onto the span of eigenvectors with negative eigenvalue, and define W-(v) := ||P- w||^2, M1-(v) := w^T A(H) P- w, M2-(v) := w^T A(H)^2 P- w, and I(v) := W-(v) + (M1-(v))^2 / M2-(v) if M2-(v) > 0, else I(v) := W-(v). Conjecture (condition (a), with T := 0.4122 = 2061/5000): for every 2-tree G on n >= 4 vertices there exists a simplicial degree-2 ear v* attaining the maximum degsum (as in row maxdegsum-selector) with I(v*) >= T.

rows.title: (L') existential ear-selection lemma for 2-trees
rows.statement_text: Definitions: for a finite simple graph G with adjacency matrix A(G), s+(G) (resp. s-(G)) is the sum of the squares of the positive (resp. negative) eigenvalues of A(G). A 2-tree is defined recursively: K_3 is a 2-tree, and any graph obtained from a 2-tree by adding one new vertex adjacent to exactly the two endpoints of an existing edge is a 2-tree. A simplicial degree-2 ear of a 2-tree G is a vertex v with deg_G(v)=2 whose two neighbours are adjacent; then G-v is again a 2-tree. For such v set delta+(v) := s+(G) - s+(G-v) and delta-(v) := s-(G) - s-(G-v). Conjecture (L'): for every 2-tree G on n >= 4 vertices there exists a simplicial degree-2 ear v* with delta+(v*) >= 17/16 and delta-(v*) >= 17/16 (equivalently, by the trace identity delta+(v*) + delta-(v*) = 4, with delta-(v*) in [17/16, 47/16]).

rows.statement_text: Let L_n (the 2-path, the square of the path P_n) be the graph on vertex set {1,...,n} with i adjacent to j iff |i-j| in {1,2}; then L_n is a 2-tree and L_n minus the vertex n is L_{n-1}. Define delta-(L_n) := s-(L_n) - s-(L_{n-1}) with s- as in row lprime. Claim: for every integer n >= 4, delta-(L_n) >= 17/16.

rows.title: Universal ear-deletion lemma (L) — refuted by BT(k,2) tail ears
rows.statement_text: With definitions as in row lprime: for every 2-tree G on n >= 4 vertices and every simplicial degree-2 ear v of G, min(delta+(v), delta-(v)) >= 17/16. [REFUTED. Counterexample: the 2-tree BT(50,2) on n = 54 vertices — vertices 0,1 (book spine), 2..51 (book pages adjacent to both 0 and 1), plus edges {0,52},{2,52},{2,53},{52,53} — whose tail ear v = 53 (supporting edge {2,52}) has delta-(v) ~= 1.05751 < 17/16 = 1.0625; the BT(100,2) analogue on n = 104 has delta- ~= 1.04716.]

rows.title: Single-scalar W- threshold at 17/32 (retired Conjecture 7.1, natural instance) — refuted on 2-paths
rows.statement_text: With W-(v) := ||P- (e_a + e_b)||^2 defined as in row ansatz-a (P- the negative-eigenspace spectral projector of A(G-v)) and the max-degsum ear as in row maxdegsum-selector: for every 2-tree G on n >= 5 vertices, every simplicial degree-2 ear v* attaining the maximum degsum satisfies W-(v*) >= 17/32. rows.title: Conjecture L (universal form)
rows.statement_text: For every 3-arc-strong directed multigraph D (every nonempty proper X ⊂ V has |δ+(X)| ≥ 3 with multiplicity), every root r, every pair of arc-disjoint spanning in-arborescences T, U rooted at r, and every arc a ∈ T, some arc b ∈ U ∩ δ+(X_a^T) satisfies X_b^U ∩ X_a^T ⊊ X_a^T, where X_a^T = {x : the unique T-path from x to r uses a}. DISPROVED by the 4-vertex funnel pair embedded in K4* (the complete bidirected digraph on {r, u, v1, w}; 12 arcs, λ_arc = 3): T = {(v1,u),(u,r),(w,r)}, U = {(u,v1),(v1,r),(w,v1)}, a = (u,r) ∈ T, X = X_a^T = {u,v1}; the unique U-exit from X is b = (v1,r) with X_b^U = {v1,u,w}, so X_b^U ∩ X = X, not a strict subset.

rows.title: Directed Karger cut-counting DK(α)
rows.statement_text: For every λ-arc-strong directed multigraph D on n ≥ 3 vertices and every α ≥ 1, the number of nonempty proper vertex sets X ⊊ V with |δ+(X)| ≤ α·λ (arc multiplicities counted) is at most n^(2α). DISPROVED at α = 2 by the asymmetric in/out-bundle: V = {s, o, p_1, …, p_k}; arcs (s,o) and (o,s) each with multiplicity 3, and for each toggle p_i: (s,p_i) with multiplicity 3 and (p_i,o) with multiplicity 3; oracle-certified λ_arc = 3. For every S ⊆ {p_1..p_k}, the set X = {o} ∪ S has δ+(X) = the three copies of (o,s) (each toggle in S contributes 0), i.e. |δ+(X)| = 3 = λ, giving 2^k distinct sets within the α = 2 band. At k = 17 (n = 19): the band count is 131378 > n^4 = 130321.

rows.title: Directed Karger arc-set counting DK*(α) for α ≥ 4/3
rows.statement_text: For every λ-arc-strong directed multigraph D on n vertices and every α ≥ 4/3, the number of DISTINCT out-cut arc-sets {δ+(X) : ∅ ≠ X ⊊ V, |δ+(X)| ≤ α·λ} is at most n^(2α). DISPROVED by the tagged-bundle family T(k, lam): V = {s, o, p_1, …, p_k} (n = k + 2); arcs (s,o)×lam, (o,s)×lam; per toggle p_i: (s,p_i)×lam, (p_i,o)×lam, plus ONE private tag arc (p_i,s)×1. The tag arcs make S ↦ δ+({o} ∪ S) injective as an arc-set map, so the number of distinct arc-sets of size ≤ α·λ is at least Σ_{j ≤ (α−1)·lam} C(k,j) = 2^Ω(n). Oracle-certified instances: T(18,10) (n = 20, λ = 10): 199329 distinct arc-sets of size ≤ 20 > n^4 = 160000 (α = 2), and 31216 > 21715 at α = 5/3; T(22,8) (n = 24, λ = 8): 600645 arc-sets of size ≤ 16 > n^4 = 331776. Both instances are SAD = SAT, and the arc-set first-moment mass Σ_F 2^(1−|F|) exceeds 1 (2.94 / 58.7), so the union-bound route genuinely fails there.

rows.title: α = 1 core: minimum out-cut arc-set count ≤ 2(n−1)²
rows.statement_text: For every λ-arc-strong directed multigraph D on n vertices, the number of distinct global minimum out-cut arc-sets {δ+(X) : ∅ ≠ X ⊊ V, |δ+(X)| = λ_arc(D)} is at most 2(n−1)² (a fortiori at most n²). DISPROVED by the family B_k: V = {s, t, p_1, …, p_k} (n = k + 2); arcs s→p_i (×1), p_i→t (×1), p_i→s (×(k−1)), t→p_i (×(k−1)), t→s (×k). Then λ_arc(B_k) = k and B_k has exactly 2^k + 2k distinct global minimum out-cut arc-sets, 2^k of them the binary family δ+({s} ∪ S) over S ⊆ {p_1..p_k}. At k = 8 (n = 10): 272 > 2(n−1)² = 162 > n² = 100. Symbolic proof for all k ≥ 2 (four-case cut computation) plus oracle-exact λ and exhaustive arc-set enumeration at k = 6, 8.

rows.title: EPK-2: two-coordinate Edmonds-packing determination of minimum cuts
rows.statement_text: For every λ-arc-strong directed multigraph D and every root r, there exist an Edmonds packing T_1, …, T_λ of pairwise arc-disjoint spanning in-arborescences rooted at r and indices i ≠ j such that the map F ↦ (F ∩ T_i, F ∩ T_j) is injective on the family of minimum out-cut arc-sets F = δ+(X) with r ∉ X. DISPROVED by pigeonhole on B_6 (family of row G24 at k = 6, n = 8, λ = 6): by the classical Transversal Lemma (every arc-disjoint spanning in-arborescence to r crosses each root-avoiding minimum out-cut exactly once, and F ⊆ ∪T_i), each signature (F ∩ T_i, F ∩ T_j) is a pair of single arcs, one from each of two fixed (n−1)-arc trees, hence takes at most (n−1)² = 49 values for ANY packing and index pair; but B_6 has 2^6 = 64 root-avoiding minimum out-cut arc-sets (70 in total, the binary family δ+({s} ∪ S) contributing 64) — so no Edmonds packing admits an injective pair.

rows.title: L-exist for general 3-arc-strong multidigraphs
rows.statement_text: For every 3-arc-strong directed multigraph D and every arc a ∈ A(D), there exists a pair of arc-disjoint spanning in-arborescences T, U rooted at head(a) with a ∈ T such that some b ∈ U ∩ δ+(X_a^T) satisfies X_b^U ∩ X_a^T ⊊ X_a^T — even restricted to instances with 2 ≤ |X_a^T| ≤ n − 2 (notation as in row G1). DISPROVED by the path-thickening of the path 1–0–2–3 (three parallel arcs in each direction on each of the three edges; 4 vertices, 18 arcs, Eulerian, λ_arc = 3, oracle-exact): with a = any copy of (0,2), rooted at head(a) = 2, every in-arborescence containing a has X_a^T = {0,1}; every arc leaving {0,1} has tail 0, so every U has exactly one exit from X and, by the one-exit criterion, no pair has a strict exit. All 216 arc-disjoint pairs (72 ordered pairs per labelled copy of a, pairs exist so not vacuous) fail, machine-verified.

rows.title: Chain Crossing Selection / Missing Entry Lemma (sealed multi-crossing chain kernels)
rows.statement_text: Setting: D• a 3-arc-strong chord-contraction multidigraph with fixed root ρ = the contracted vertex (class as in row H2-LEXIST). Let (T,U) be arc-disjoint spanning in-arborescences rooted at ρ and a = (u,v) ∈ T such that (T,U) is a hard gateway pair at a: X_a^T equals the canonical cage C = C_u (by the proved D12 cage canonicalization C1–C7, the vertex set of a t = u hard gateway is determined by u alone, independent of the pair) and U has a unique exit arc b = (u,y) from C, so no strict U-exit exists. Let A be the T-ancestor path from v to ρ, and for w ∉ C ∪ A let S_w = {x : the T-path from x to ρ passes through w}. A realizable chain kernel is such a configuration containing a sealed block B ⊇ C with δ+(B) ⊆ {(p_i, p_{i+1}) : p_i forced}, the forced crossing arcs of the unique shortest v→ρ path P_v (computed in D• − u), where p_i is forced iff (p_i, p_{i+1}) is p_i's unique out-arc in the outside digraph D_O (the subdigraph induced on the vertices outside C ∪ A ∪ {u}); a forced crossing is U-used iff its arc lies in U; the kernel is non-degenerate (sealed multi-crossing, per the D48 classifier) iff at least two forced crossings are U-used. CONJECTURE (Missing Entry Lemma): in every realizable non-degenerate in-class chain kernel with hard gateway pair at C there is a U-used forced crossing tail s, or a T-ancestor w of such a tail inside the sealed block, satisfying: (1) w ∉ A; (2) there is an arc d = (w,c) with c ∈ C and d ∉ U (a U-free entry into the cage); (3) [y ∉ C ∪ S_w] + #{s' ∈ S_w : the U-out-arc of s' has head outside C ∪ S_w} ≥ 2. (By the proved Lemma B3+, conditions (1)-(3) imply that replacing the T-out-arc of w by d yields a good pair — a strict U-exit at a — with U unchanged; so this lemma closes the chain-kernel case of L-exist branch 2.)

A realizable chain kernel is such a configuration containing a sealed block B ⊇ C with δ+(B) ⊆ {(p_i, p_{i+1}) : p_i forced}, the forced crossing arcs of the unique shortest v→ρ path P_v (computed in D• − u), where p_i is forced iff (p_i, p_{i+1}) is p_i's unique out-arc in the outside digraph D_O (the subdigraph induced on the vertices outside C ∪ A ∪ {u}); a forced crossing is U-used iff its arc lies in U; the kernel is non-degenerate (sealed multi-crossing, per the D48 classifier) iff at least two forced crossings are U-used. CONJECTURE (Missing Entry Lemma): in every realizable non-degenerate in-class chain kernel with hard gateway pair at C there is a U-used forced crossing tail s, or a T-ancestor w of such a tail inside the sealed block, satisfying: (1) w ∉ A; (2) there is an arc d = (w,c) with c ∈ C and d ∉ U (a U-free entry into the cage); (3) [y ∉ C ∪ S_w] + #{s' ∈ S_w : the U-out-arc of s' has head outside C ∪ S_w} ≥ 2. (By the proved Lemma B3+, conditions (1)-(3) imply that replacing the T-out-arc of w by d yields a good pair — a strict U-exit at a — with U unchanged; so this lemma closes the chain-kernel case of L-exist branch 2.)

rows.title: L-exist (chord-contraction class, fixed contracted root)
rows.statement_text: Let D be a simple 3-arc-strong (1,0)-near-split digraph: V(D) = V1 ⊔ V2, D[V2] semicomplete (every two distinct vertices of V2 joined by an arc in at least one direction), |V2| ≥ 3, and V1 carrying exactly one internal arc e0 = (p,q) ('3-arc-strong' = every nonempty proper X ⊂ V has |δ+(X)| ≥ 3, arcs counted with multiplicity). Let D• be the chord-contraction multidigraph obtained from D by contracting e0 to a single vertex r (identify p,q; delete loops; keep parallel arcs), and assume λ_arc(D•) ≥ 3. For an in-arborescence T rooted at r (a spanning arc set giving every vertex ≠ r exactly one out-arc, with all T-paths leading to r) and an arc a ∈ T, write X_a^T = {x ∈ V(D•) : the unique T-path from x to r uses a}. CONJECTURE: for every arc a ∈ A(D•) there exist arc-disjoint spanning in-arborescences T, U of D• rooted at r with a ∈ T such that, whenever 2 ≤ |X_a^T| ≤ |V(D•)| − 2, some arc b ∈ U ∩ δ+(X_a^T) satisfies X_b^U ∩ X_a^T ⊊ X_a^T (equivalently, by the proved one-exit criterion Lemma 2.1, |U ∩ δ+(X_a^T)| ≥ 2).

rows.title: Constant-λ Eulerian strong-arc-decomposition theorem
rows.statement_text: There exists an absolute constant c such that every Eulerian directed multigraph D (d+(v) = d−(v) for every vertex v) with λ_arc(D) ≥ c (every nonempty proper X ⊂ V has |δ+(X)| ≥ c, arc multiplicities counted) admits a strong arc decomposition (SAD): a partition A(D) = A1 ⊔ A2 such that both spanning subdigraphs (V, A1) and (V, A2) are strongly connected. Falsifiable instance form: a single Eulerian c-arc-strong (for the fixed c, e.g. c = 3) digraph with no SAD refutes the c-instance and, at c = 3, refutes WC3 in the Eulerian world.

rows.title: Interface-width merge lemma (refuted): width >= 3 per side of a digon-free 2/2 cut forces 2-dicolourability
rows.statement_text: Setting: D a finite loopless digraph without parallel arcs; digon = pair of opposite arcs; single arc = arc uv with vu absent; D Eulerian = in-degree equals out-degree at every vertex; lambda(D) = max over ordered pairs of the max number of pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths; chi_vec(D) = least t with V(D) partitioned into t classes inducing acyclic subdigraphs. For a digon-free cut (S, V(D)\S) (both sides nonempty, no digon crossing), the crossing arcs are the arcs with one end in each side, and the interface-width of a side is the number of distinct endpoints of crossing arcs lying on that side. REFUTED CLAIM: if D is Eulerian with lambda(D) = 2 and has a digon-free cut with exactly two crossing arcs S -> V(D)\S, exactly two crossing arcs V(D)\S -> S, and interface-width >= 3 on each side, then chi_vec(D) <= 2. (Companion refuted claim, killed by the same witness: for such digraphs, interface-width >= 3 on each side of such a cut implies U(D) is 3-connected.)

rows.title: P4 overlap target: the overlapping pure-point four-cycle cover is impossible at k(F_D)=3
rows.statement_text: Setting: D a finite loopless digraph without parallel arcs; digon = pair of opposite arcs uv,vu; single arc = arc uv with vu absent; U(D) = underlying simple graph; F_D = undirected graph on V(D) with edges the digon pairs; lambda(D) = max over ordered pairs of the max number of pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths; chi_vec(D) = least t with V(D) partitioned into t classes inducing acyclic subdigraphs; D is 2-extremal iff D is strongly connected, U(D) is 2-connected, lambda(D)=2 and chi_vec(D)=3. For 2-extremal D, F_D is a forest (proved in-folder, docs/lemma_a.md), so if F_D has exactly 3 connected components (isolated vertices counted) its proper 2-colourings (digon ends coloured differently) modulo global colour swap form the flip set Omega with |Omega| = 4. Let S be the spanning subdigraph of D consisting of all single arcs. A directed cycle of S is BAD AT x in Omega if all its vertices receive one colour under x, and FULL-SUPPORT if it has vertices in all three F_D-components. CLAIM: there is no 2-extremal digraph D with U(D) 3-connected and F_D having exactly 3 components such that (a) no bad dicycle of S has vertices in exactly two F_D-components, (b) there exist four full-support dicycles {C_x : x in Omega}, C_x bad at x, with union of arc sets equal to A(S), and (c) the C_x are not pairwise arc-disjoint, i.e. the overlap circulation Sum_{x in Omega} 1_{C_x} - 1_S is nonzero. Equivalently, such a configuration forces lambda(D) >= 3, contradicting lambda(D) = 2.

rows.title: Connectivity-form hub barrier (refuted): uniform 4-edge-connectivity forces a connected digon forest
rows.statement_text: Setting: D a finite loopless digraph without parallel arcs; digon = pair of opposite arcs uv,vu; single arc = arc uv with vu absent; U(D) = underlying simple undirected graph; F_D = undirected graph on V(D) with edges the digon pairs; D Eulerian = in-degree equals out-degree at every vertex; lambda(D) = max over ordered pairs of the max number of pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths. Let M be the undirected multigraph obtained from U(D) by replacing each digon {u,v} by two parallel u-v edges and each single arc by one edge; M is uniformly 4-edge-connected if every pair of distinct vertices is joined by exactly 4 pairwise edge-disjoint paths in M. REFUTED CLAIM: if U(D) is 3-connected, D is Eulerian, lambda(D) = 2, and M is uniformly 4-edge-connected, then F_D is connected (equivalently, D has no digon-free cut).

rows.title: Criticality barrier: a 3-connected lambda=2 Eulerian digraph with a digon-free cut is 2-dicolourable
rows.statement_text: Let D be a finite loopless digraph with no parallel arcs (a digon is a pair of opposite arcs uv and vu). Let U(D) be its underlying simple undirected graph and F_D the undirected graph on V(D) whose edges are exactly the vertex pairs joined by a digon of D. For an ordered pair (x,y), lambda(x,y) is the maximum number of pairwise arc-disjoint directed x->y paths, and lambda(D) = max over all ordered pairs (x,y) of lambda(x,y). The dichromatic number chi_vec(D) is the least t such that V(D) can be partitioned into t classes each inducing an acyclic subdigraph. D is Eulerian if in-degree equals out-degree at every vertex. A digon-free cut is a bipartition (S, V(D)\S) with both sides nonempty such that no digon has one end in each side; such a cut exists iff F_D is disconnected as a graph on all of V(D) (isolated vertices count as components). CLAIM: for every such D, if (i) U(D) is 3-connected, (ii) D is Eulerian, (iii) lambda(D) = 2, and (iv) D has a digon-free cut, then chi_vec(D) <= 2. Equivalently: if U(D) is 3-connected, D is Eulerian, lambda(D) = 2 and chi_vec(D) = 3, then F_D is connected.

rows.title: BST-orderings are free on the S_k tower (bstOmega(S_k) = omegaVec(S_k) for k <= 4)
rows.statement_text: For every k in {1,2,3,4}, bstOmega(S_k) = omegaVec(S_k). Definitions: S_1 = TT1 (one-vertex tournament), S_k = Delta(TT1, S_{k-1}, S_{k-1}), where Delta(A,B,C) is the substitution of tournaments A, B, C into the directed triangle (disjoint union of V(A), V(B), V(C), internal arcs kept, plus all arcs a->b, b->c, c->a for a in V(A), b in V(B), c in V(C)). For a linear ordering prec of V(T), the back-edge graph of (T,prec) is the undirected graph on V(T) with an edge {u,w} for u prec w iff T contains the arc w->u; omegaVec(T) is the minimum over ALL linear orderings prec of the clique number of the back-edge graph of (T,prec). A BST-ordering of T is defined recursively: choose a root r in V(T); the ordering is (a BST-ordering of the subtournament induced on N^-(r) = {u : u->r}), then r, then (a BST-ordering of the subtournament induced on N^+(r) = {u : r->u}); bstOmega(T) is the minimum over BST-orderings prec of T of the clique number of the back-edge graph of (T,prec) (so bstOmega(T) >= omegaVec(T) always).

rows.title: chiVec = omegaVec on prime twin-width-<=1 tournaments
rows.statement_text: Every prime tournament T with tww(T) <= 1 satisfies chiVec(T) = omegaVec(T). Definitions: a tournament is a finite loopless directed graph with exactly one arc between every pair of distinct vertices. A module of T is a vertex set M such that every vertex v outside M satisfies either v->m in T for all m in M, or m->v in T for all m in M; T is prime if it has no module M with 1 < |M| < |V(T)|. chiVec(T), the dichromatic number, is the least r such that V(T) can be partitioned into r sets each inducing an acyclic subtournament. omegaVec(T) is the minimum over all linear orderings prec of V(T) of the clique number of the back-edge graph of (T,prec), the undirected graph on V(T) with an edge {u,w} for u prec w iff T contains the arc w->u. tww(T) (twin-width) is defined via contraction sequences: a sequence of partitions of V(T) starting from singletons, each step merging two parts, ending in one part; at any step two distinct parts P, P' carry a red edge unless they are homogeneous (every arc of T between P and P' goes from P to P', or every such arc goes from P' to P); the width of a sequence is the maximum over steps and parts of the number of red edges at a part, and tww(T) is the minimum width over all contraction sequences.

rows.title: Transitive-middle substitution tower R_k keeps omegaVec <= 2
rows.statement_text: For every k >= 1, omegaVec(R_k) <= 2, where the tournaments R_k are defined by R_1 = TT1 (the one-vertex tournament) and R_k = Delta(R_{k-1}, TT_{k-1}, R_{k-1}); here TT_m is the transitive tournament on m vertices (vertices 1..m with arc i->j iff i < j), and Delta(A,B,C) is the substitution of tournaments A, B, C into the directed triangle: the tournament on the disjoint union of V(A), V(B), V(C) keeping all arcs internal to A, B, C, plus every arc a->b, b->c, c->a for a in V(A), b in V(B), c in V(C). omegaVec(T) is the minimum over all linear orderings prec of V(T) of the clique number of the back-edge graph of (T,prec), the undirected graph on V(T) with an edge {u,w} for u prec w iff T contains the arc w->u. (Proposed so that {R_k} — with twin-width 1 and growing dichromatic number chiVec(R_k) — would be a bounded-omegaVec counterexample family to Conjecture 3.12.)

rows.title: C = 2 deletion bound for internal vertices (unavoidability)
rows.statement_text: For every finite acyclic digraph D and every vertex v of D having at least one in-neighbour and at least one out-neighbour (an 'internal' vertex), unvd(D) <= 2 * unvd(D - v). Here a tournament is an orientation of a complete graph (exactly one arc between every pair of distinct vertices); a tournament T contains a digraph H if there is an injective map f: V(H) -> V(T) such that (u,w) in A(H) implies (f(u),f(w)) in A(T); and for a nonempty acyclic digraph H, unvd(H) (the unavoidability of H) is the least integer p >= 1 such that every tournament on p vertices contains H (finite for every acyclic H). D - v denotes the digraph obtained from D by deleting v and all arcs incident to v.

rows.statement_text: For every integer k >= 3, the flower snark J_{2k+1} (defined as in row flower-family) has cyclic edge-connectivity at least 6, where the cyclic edge-connectivity of a cubic graph containing two vertex-disjoint cycles is the minimum size of an edge cut whose removal leaves at least two components each containing a cycle. (Companion finite fact, machine-verified in the folder: J_5 has cyclic edge-connectivity exactly 5.)

rows.title: Flower snarks J_{2k+1} all admit S2-flows (infinite-family target)
rows.statement_text: For every integer k >= 2, the flower snark J_{2k+1} admits an S2-flow. Definitions: for odd n = 2k+1, the flower snark J_n is the cubic graph on vertex set {a_i, b_i, c_i, d_i : i in Z/n} with edges a_i b_i, a_i c_i, a_i d_i (spokes, for every i), b_i b_{i+1 mod n} (the b-cycle), c_i c_{i+1} and d_i d_{i+1} for 0 <= i <= n-2, and the two cross edges c_{n-1} d_0 and d_{n-1} c_0 (so c_0 ... c_{n-1} d_0 ... d_{n-1} form a single 2n-cycle); J_n is simple, cubic, bridgeless, of girth 5 for n >= 5, and not 3-edge-colourable. Fix a reference orientation of each edge (for e = {u,v} with u < v set sigma(u,e) = +1, sigma(v,e) = -1). An S2-flow on a graph G is a map phi : E(G) -> S2 = {x in R^3 : |x| = 1} such that for every vertex v, sum over edges e incident to v of sigma(v,e) * phi(e) = 0 in R^3 (Kirchhoff conservation).

rows.title: Uniform shuttle CDC for flower snarks (refuted parametric template)
rows.statement_text: [REFUTED HYPOTHESIS] For every odd n = 2k+1 >= 5, the flower snark J_n (defined as in row flower-family) admits a cycle double cover (a multiset of cycles covering every edge exactly twice) in which every cycle passing through a star vertex a_i is a length-6 shuttle, where the shuttle of type bc at index i is the 6-cycle a_i b_i b_{i+1} a_{i+1} c_{i+1} c_i and the types bd and cd are defined analogously (indices mod n; at the wrap-around index the shuttle uses the cross edges c_{n-1} d_0 / d_{n-1} c_0). Concrete candidates refuted: v1 = {b-cycle, cd-cycle, all bc-shuttles, all bd-shuttles} and v2 = {all bc-shuttles, all bd-shuttles with cross-edge wrap-around} (scripts/flower_cdc.py).

rows.title: Z/(2n)-equivariant S2-flow on flower snarks (refuted ansatz)
rows.statement_text: [REFUTED HYPOTHESIS] For odd n = 2k+1 >= 5, the flower snark J_n (defined as in row flower-family) admits a Z/(2n)-equivariant S2-flow: there exist a rotation R in SO(3) of order exactly 2n (rotation by pi/n about some axis) and unit vectors u_b, u_c, w_b, w_c in S2 such that the assignment phi(a_i b_i) = R^i u_b, phi(a_i c_i) = R^i u_c, phi(a_i d_i) = R^{n+i} u_c, phi(b_i b_{i+1 mod n}) = R^i w_b (0 <= i <= n-1), and phi(sigma^j(c_0 c_1)) = R^j w_c (0 <= j <= 2n-1, where sigma is the order-2n graph automorphism of J_n shifting the cd-cycle by one step and the a/b indices by one mod n) is an S2-flow on J_n.

rows.title: No Z/n-equivariant S2-flow on flower snarks (nonexistence, uncertified)
rows.statement_text: For every odd n in {5, 7, 9, 11, 13} (working hypothesis: every odd n >= 5), the flower snark J_n (defined as in row flower-family) admits no partially Z/n-equivariant S2-flow. Precisely: there exist NO unit vectors u_b, u_c, u_d, w_b, w_c, w_d, x_cd, x_dc in S2 and unit axis a in S2, with R in SO(3) the rotation by angle 2*pi/n about a, satisfying the system: u_b + u_c + u_d = 0; u_b = (I - R^{-1}) w_b; u_c = (I - R^{-1}) w_c; u_d = (I - R^{-1}) w_d; u_c + x_dc = w_c; u_d + x_cd = w_d; R^{n-1} u_c + R^{n-2} w_c = x_cd; R^{n-1} u_d + R^{n-2} w_d = x_dc. A solution of this system is exactly an S2-flow on J_n of the form phi(a_i b_i) = R^i u_b, phi(a_i c_i) = R^i u_c, phi(a_i d_i) = R^i u_d, phi(b_i b_{i+1 mod n}) = R^i w_b, phi(c_i c_{i+1}) = R^i w_c and phi(d_i d_{i+1}) = R^i w_d (0 <= i <= n-2), with standalone values x_cd on cross edge c_{n-1} d_0 and x_dc on cross edge d_{n-1} c_0 (33 scalar equations in 27 real variables, over-determined by 6).

rows.title: Some snark admits an oriented 4-CDC (refuted route hypothesis)
rows.statement_text: [REFUTED HYPOTHESIS] There exists a snark (a simple connected cubic bridgeless graph with chromatic index 4) admitting an oriented 4-cycle double cover, i.e. a collection of exactly 4 directed cycles such that every edge is covered exactly twice and the two covering cycles traverse it in opposite directions. (This was the enabling hypothesis of the first-draft working theorem 'if a snark admits an oriented 4-CDC then it admits an S2-flow' - formally true but vacuous, since the hypothesis is unsatisfiable.)

rows.title: Blanusa-1 admits a weighted-CDC Sigma_4 flow (abstraction-gap probe)
rows.statement_text: The first Blanusa snark B1 (one of the two nontrivial snarks on 18 vertices; a nontrivial snark is a simple connected cubic bridgeless graph with chromatic index 4, girth >= 5, cyclically 4-edge-connected) admits a weighted-CDC Sigma_4-flow: there exist a cycle double cover C = {C_1, ..., C_t} of B1 (a multiset of cycles such that every edge lies in exactly two members), a direction for each cycle C_k, and vectors w_1, ..., w_t in R^4 each satisfying sum_{i=1}^4 (w_k)_i = 0, such that for every edge e - covered by exactly the two cycles C_i and C_j - the vector v_e := sigma_{e,i} w_i + sigma_{e,j} w_j lies in Sigma_4 := {x in R^4 : sum_i x_i = 0, sum_i x_i^2 = 2}, where sigma_{e,k} = +1 if the directed cycle C_k traverses e in the direction of the fixed reference orientation of e and -1 otherwise. (Sigma_4 is the radius-sqrt(2) sphere in the hyperplane sum x_i = 0, isomorphic to R^3, so any solution projects to an S2-flow on B1.)

rows.title: Erdős problem #1155

rows.statement_text: Construct a random graph on $n$ vertices in the following way: begin with the complete graph $K_n$. At each stage, choose uniformly a random triangle in the graph and delete all the edges of this triangle. Repeat until the graph is triangle-free. In particular, if $f(n)$ is the number of edges remaining, then is it true that\[\mathbb{E}f(n)\asymp n^{3/2}\]and that $f(n) \ll n^{3/2}$ almost surely?

rows.title: Erdős problem #778
rows.prize: OPEN This is open, and cannot be resolved with a finite computation.
rows.statement_text: Alice and Bob play a game on the edges of $K_n$, alternating colouring edges by red (Alice) and blue (Bob). Alice goes first, and wins if at the end the largest red clique is larger than any of the blue cliques. Does Bob have a winning strategy for $n\geq 3$? (Erdős believed the answer is yes.) If we change the game so that Bob colours two edges after each edge that Alice colours, but now require Bob's largest clique to be strictly larger than Alice's, then does Bob have a winning strategy for $n>3$? Finally, consider the game when Alice wins if the maximum degree of the red subgraph is larger than the maximum degree of the blue subgraph. Who wins?

rows.title: Meyniel's conjecture on the cop number
rows.statement_text: There is an absolute constant $C$ such that every connected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices has cop number $c(G) \le C\sqrt{n}$.
rows.context_text: In the game of Cops and Robbers, $k$ cops choose vertices, then the robber chooses a vertex, and the two sides alternate moves (cops first), each piece moving to a vertex at distance at most one; the cops win if a cop occupies the robber's vertex. The cop number $c(G)$ is the least $k$ for which the cops have a winning strategy. Writing $c(n)$ for the maximum of $c(G)$ over connected graphs of order $n$, the conjecture says $c(n) = O(\sqrt{n})$; it is equivalent to $M_k = \Omega(k^2)$, where $M_k$ is the minimum order of a connected graph with cop number $k$ (Baird et al. 2014). The bound would be tight up to the constant: incidence graphs of projective planes give $c(n) \ge \sqrt{n/2} - o(\sqrt n)$.
rows.source_text: There is an absolute constant $C$ such that every connected graph $G$ on $n$ vertices has cop number $c(G) \le C\sqrt{n}$.

rows.verification_note: Authored in X217.v:meyniel_cop_number_sqrt_statement. Meyniel: one absolute constant C bounds the cop number of every connected nonempty graph by C * sqrt_ceil(n). New shared foundation graph-theory-misc/theories/foundations/cops.v (self-contained, generic over an sgraph, also intended for the hypergraph-theory half of X217): cop_position k = {ffun 'I_k -> G}, captured/cop_move/robber_move, the boolean bounded-horizon cops_capture t C r (cops move first, a cop landing on the robber ends the play), cops_win_within k t, cops_win k = exists t, cops_win_within k t, and cop_number_le k = exists j <
rows.status_semantics: Meyniel's conjecture (c(G) ≤ C√n for every connected n-vertex graph) remains open. The best known general upper bound is n · 2^{-(1-o(1))√log₂ n}, proved independently by Lu–Peng (2012) and Scott–Sudakov (2011); the weak Meyniel conjecture (c(G) = O(n^{1−ε}) for some ε > 0) is also open for general graphs. Recent work has verified the full conjecture for dense large-girth graphs (minimum degree δ ≥ n^{2/g+ε}) and the weak form for algebraic graphs including Cayley sum and generalised Cayley graphs; a 2026 paper proves the hypergraph analogue c(H) = O(√(n/k)) for expanding hypergraphs and with high probability for random k-uniform hypergraphs under density conditions.

rows.title: Coarse Menger conjecture
rows.statement_text: For all integers $k,c\geq 1$ there exists $\ell>0$ with the following property. Let $G$ be a graph and let $S,T\subseteq V(G)$. rows.title: Erdős–Hajnal Conjecture
rows.statement_text: For every hereditary property $\mathcal{P}$ which is not satisfied by all graphs, there exists a constant $\varepsilon(\mathcal{P}) > 0$ such that every graph of $n$ vertices with property $\mathcal{P}$ has a clique or an independent set of size at least $n^{\varepsilon(\mathcal{P})}$.

rows.title: Erdős–Hajnal conjecture (coherent reformulation)

rows.class_notes: Explicitly a coherent reformulation of Erdős–Hajnal (ω·α ≥ n^c is the standard equivalent form); the canonical EH conjecture is tracked at opg:the_erdos_hajnal_conjecture.

rows.title: Harary–Hill Conjecture
rows.statement_text: The minimum number of crossings in any drawing of the complete graph $K_n$ in the plane is $$H(n) = \frac{1}{4} \left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-1}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-2}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-3}{2} \right\rfloor = \begin{cases} \frac{1}{64} n(n-2)^2(n-4), & n \text{ even};\\ \frac{1}{64}(n-1)^2(n-3)^2, & n \text{ odd.} \end{cases}$$
rows.license: arXiv-derived (studies-role extraction; per-paper license at REC time)
rows.class_notes: The OPG row states cr(K_n)=1/4·floor(n/2)floor((n-1)/2)floor((n-2)/2)floor((n-3)/2), which is exactly the Hill/Harary–Hill formula in the cluster statement.

rows.source_text: For every simple graph $G$, for any integer $k > \chi'(G)$, for any $k$-edge-colouring $\alpha$, is there a $\chi'(G)$-edge-colouring that can be reached from $\alpha$ through a series of Kempe changes?
rows.license: arXiv-derived (studies-role extraction; per-paper license at REC time)
rows.class_notes: Vizing's question that any k-edge-colouring (k > chi') can reach a chi'-edge-colouring via Kempe changes; candidates (opg:a_generalization_of_vizings_theorem is a hypergraph statement, others unrelated) do not match; needs a Kempe-change reachability primitive.

rows.title: Vizing's List Edge Colouring Conjecture
rows.statement_text: $\mathrm{ch}'(G) \leq \Delta(G) + 1$ for any graph $G$.
rows.license: arXiv-derived (studies-role extraction; per-paper license at REC time)
rows.class_notes: Vizing's list edge chromatic conjecture (ch'(G) <= Delta+1) is the list edge colouring conjecture tracked as opg:edge_list_coloring_conjecture (ch' = chi'), the standard named target; matcher missed it here but listed it for the identical cluster 548.

rows.title: Vizing's List Edge Colouring Conjecture
rows.statement_text: Every simple graph $G$ satisfies $\chi'_\ell(G) \leq \Delta(G) + 1$.
rows.license: arXiv-derived (studies-role extraction; per-paper license at REC time)
rows.class_notes: chi'_ell(G) <= Delta+1 is Vizing's list edge colouring conjecture, aliased to opg:edge_list_coloring_conjecture (listed candidate).

rows.title: Walther–Zamfirescu longest-path-transversal question
rows.statement_text: Does there exist an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that every connected graph $G$ satisfies $\mathrm{lpt}(G) \leq c$?

rows.title: Weak Coarse Menger Conjecture (Nguyen–Scott–Seymour)
rows.statement_text: For all integers $k,c\geq 1$ there exist $m,\ell>0$ with the following property. Let $G$ be a graph and let $S,T\subseteq V(G)$. Then either there are $k$ paths between $S,T$, pairwise at distance at least $c$; or there is a set $X\subseteq V(G)$ with $|X|\leq m$ such that every path between $S,T$ contains a vertex with distance at most $\ell$ from some member of $X$.
rows.source_text: For all integers $k,c\geq 1$ there exist $m,\ell>0$ with the following property. Let $G$ be a graph and let $S,T\subseteq V(G)$. Then either there are $k$ paths between $S,T$, pairwise at distance at least $c$; or there is a set $X\subseteq V(G)$ with $|X|\leq m$ such that every path between $S,T$ contains a vertex with distance at most $\ell$ from some member of $X$.
rows.license: arXiv-derived (studies-role extraction; per-paper license at REC time)
rows.class_notes: General Weak Coarse Menger conjecture (all k,c); candidates are only restricted/special cases (arxiv:2509.07174 surfaces, arxiv:2508.14332#00 c=2 open case, arxiv:2309.07905 bounded-degree), so the general statement is untracked; needs path-distance primitives.

rows.title: Weak Meyniel's Conjecture
rows.statement_text: There is an $\varepsilon > 0$ such that every graph $G$ of order $n$ has $c(G) = O(n^{1-\varepsilon})$.
rows.source_text: There is an $\varepsilon > 0$ such that every graph $G$ of order $n$ has $c(G) = O(n^{1-\varepsilon})$.
rows.license: arXiv-derived (studies-role extraction; per-paper license at REC time)
rows.class_notes: Famous conjecture that the cop number satisfies c(G) = O(n^{1-eps}) for some eps>0; all candidates (Jaeger flow variant, weak pentagon, derived FAS row, directed tree-width) are unrelated; sublinear asymptotic growth claim.

rows.title: Wigderson's Edge-Deletion Ramsey Conjecture
rows.statement_text: Deleting an edge from a graph can change the Ramsey number by at most a constant factor.
rows.source_text: Deleting an edge from a graph can change the Ramsey number by at most a constant factor.
rows.license: arXiv-derived (studies-role extraction; per-paper license at REC time)
rows.class_notes: Named crisp conjecture that deleting one edge changes the Ramsey number by at most a constant factor; opg edge-colouring/packing candidates are unrelated, and Ramsey numbers sit in extremal-graph-theory.

rows.title: Wood's Conjecture on Pathwidth and Binary-Tree Subdivisions
rows.statement_text: Every graph with treewidth $t$ and not containing a subdivision of a complete binary tree of height $h$ has pathwidth at most $f(t) \cdot h$ for some function $f$.
rows.source_text: Every graph with treewidth $t$ and not containing a subdivision of a complete binary tree of height $h$ has pathwidth at most $f(t) \cdot h$ for some function $f$.
rows.license: arXiv-derived (studies-role extraction; per-paper license at REC time)
rows.class_notes: Named width-parameter conjecture (bounded treewidth + no height-h binary-tree subdivision ⇒ pathwidth ≤ f(t)·h); no candidate matches and treewidth/pathwidth/subdivision are minor-theory primitives.

rows.title: Wood's Conjecture on the Maximum Number of Cliques in Kₜ-Minor-Free Graphs
rows.statement_text: The maximum number of cliques a $K_t$-minor free graph on $n$ vertices can have is $2^{t-2}(n-t+3)$ if and only if $t \leq 49$.
rows.source_text: The maximum number of cliques a $K_t$-minor free graph on $n$ vertices can have is $2^{t-2}(n-t+3)$ if and only if $t \leq 49$.
rows.license: arXiv-derived (studies-role extraction; per-paper license at REC time)
rows.class_notes: Named exact extremal conjecture (max cliques = 2^{t-2}(n-t+3) iff t ≤ 49); distinct from the weaker asymptotic opg 'cliques in minor-closed classes' question, so promote under minor-theory.

rows.title: Wood's Open Problem 18 (Clustered Choosability of Bounded-Degree Graphs on Surfaces)
rows.statement_text: Consider a surface $\Sigma$ and a positive integer $\Delta$. Is it true that the class of graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$ than can be drawn on $\Sigma$ has clustered choosability at most three?
rows.source_text: Consider a surface $\Sigma$ and a positive integer $\Delta$. Is it true that the class of graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$ than can be drawn on $\Sigma$ has clustered choosability at most three?
rows.license: arXiv-derived (studies-role extraction; per-paper license at REC time)
rows.class_notes: Named survey open problem (Wood, OP 18) studied by arXiv:2111.07147 on weak-diameter/clustered coloring on surfaces; no candidate matches, and surface embeddings put it under chromatic-theory/needs-planarity.

rows.title: Wood–Telle Conjecture (Σ deg² Crossing-Number Bound for Minor-Free Graphs)
rows.statement_text: For every graph $H$, there is a constant $c = c(H)$ such that every $H$-minor-free graph $G$ has crossing number $\mathrm{cr}(G) \leq c \sum_{v \in V(G)} \deg(v)^2$.
rows.source_text: For every graph $H$, there is a constant $c = c(H)$ such that every $H$-minor-free graph $G$ has crossing number $\mathrm{cr}(G) \leq c \sum_{v \in V(G)} \deg(v)^2$.
rows.license: arXiv-derived (studies-role extraction; per-paper license at REC time)
rows.class_notes: Named crisp conjecture bounding cr(G) by c·Σdeg² for H-minor-free graphs; opg 'notions of crossing number' and the others do not match, and crossing number is topological-graph-theory/needs-planarity.

rows.title: Wood–Telle Question (Linear c·Δ·n Crossing-Number Bound for Minor-Free Graphs)
rows.statement_text: Is it true that for every graph $H$ there is a constant $c = c(H)$ such that every $H$-minor-free graph $G$ has crossing number $\mathrm{cr}(G) \leq c \cdot \Delta(G) \cdot |G|$?
rows.source_text: Is it true that for every graph $H$ there is a constant $c = c(H)$ such that every $H$-minor-free graph $G$ has crossing number $\mathrm{cr}(G) \leq c \cdot \Delta(G) \cdot |G|$?
rows.license: arXiv-derived (studies-role extraction; per-paper license at REC time)
rows.class_notes: Distinct named Wood–Telle open question (cr(G) ≤ c·Δ(G)·|G|) from the same paper; erdos:619 is a triangle-free diameter problem and other candidates are unrelated, so promote as a separate crossing-number target.

rows.title: Woodall's List-Colouring Conjecture for Kₛ,ₜ-Minor-Free Graphs
rows.statement_text: For every $s, t \in \mathbb{N}$, if $G$ is a graph with $G \not\succeq K_{s,t}$, then $\chi_{\ell}(G) \leq s + t - 1$.
rows.source_text: For every $s, t \in \mathbb{N}$, if $G$ is a graph with $G \not\succeq K_{s,t}$, then $\chi_{\ell}(G) \leq s + t - 1$.
rows.license: arXiv-derived (studies-role extraction; per-paper license at REC time)
rows.verification_note: Authored in X12.v:woodall_ks_t_minor_free_list_colouring_statement. Encodes Woodall's list-colouring conjecture: for all positive s,t, every K_{s,t}-minor-free graph has choice number at most s+t-1.
rows.class_notes: List-Hadwiger-type conjecture (Kₛ,ₜ-minor-free ⇒ χ_ℓ ≤ s+t−1); opg:woodalls_conjecture is the unrelated dijoin conjecture and arxiv:2201.09115#01 is the paper's weaker 2s+t question, so promote under the existing list-hadwiger topic.

rows.title: Yang's Conjecture (Two-Simultaneous-Cops Cop Number of Planar Graphs)
rows.statement_text: For any planar graph $G$, $c_2(G) \leq 3$.
rows.source_text: For any planar graph $G$, $c_2(G) \leq 3$.
rows.license: arXiv-derived (studies-role extraction; per-paper license at REC time)
rows.class_notes: Named pursuit-game conjecture proved by arXiv:2406.01068 (c₂ = cop number when ≤2 cops move per round; c₂ ≤ 3 for planar graphs); no candidate matches, filed with the cops-and-robbers convention.

rows.title: Yao–Zhou Conjecture on the Edge Density of 4-Critical Planar Graphs
rows.statement_text: $L := \limsup_{G\,4\text{-critical planar}} |E(G)|/|V(G)| = 7/3$.
rows.source_text: $L := \limsup_{G\,4\text{-critical planar}} |E(G)|/|V(G)| = 7/3$.
rows.license: arXiv-derived (studies-role extraction; per-paper license at REC time)
rows.class_notes: Named conjecture that limsup |E|/|V| = 7/3 over 4-critical planar graphs; opg edge-critical/list candidates and the 12-critical earth-moon derived row are different statements, so promote as a planar colour-critical density target.

rows.title: You–Liu / Zhai–Shu–Hong Conjecture on Algebraic Connectivity of a Graph and its Complement
rows.statement_text: For any graph $G$ of order $n \geq 2$, the following holds: $$\lambda_n(G) - \lambda_2(G) \leq n - 1,$$ or equivalently $\lambda_2(G) + \lambda_2(\bar{G}) \geq 1$, with equality if and only if $G$ or $\bar{G}$ is isomorphic to the join of an isolated vertex and a disconnected graph of order $n - 1$.
rows.source_text: For any graph $G$ of order $n \geq 2$, the following holds: $$\lambda_n(G) - \lambda_2(G) \leq n - 1,$$ or equivalently $\lambda_2(G) + \lambda_2(\bar{G}) \geq 1$, with equality if and only if $G$ or $\bar{G}$ is isomorphic to the join of an isolated vertex and a disconnected graph of order $n - 1$.
rows.license: arXiv-derived (studies-role extraction; per-paper license at REC time)
rows.class_notes: Named Laplacian-eigenvalue conjecture (λ₂(G)+λ₂(Ḡ) ≥ 1, with equality characterization) from arXiv:1806.06770; candidates (digraph colouring, coarse Menger, group flows) are unrelated, so promote under spectral-graph-theory.
rows.attributed_to: You and Liu; Zhai, Shu, and Hong

rows.title: Ziegler–Drewnowski–Łuczak–Alon Conjecture on the Chromatic Number of r-Stable Kneser Hypergraphs
rows.statement_text: The chromatic number of $KG^r(k, n)_{r-\mathrm{stab}}$ is $\left\lceil \dfrac{n - r(k-1)}{r-1} \right\rceil$, the same as the chromatic number of the full Kneser hypergraph $KG^r(k, n)$.
rows.source_text: The chromatic number of $KG^r(k, n)_{r-\mathrm{stab}}$ is $\left\lceil \dfrac{n - r(k-1)}{r-1} \right\rceil$, the same as the chromatic number of the full Kneser hypergraph $KG^r(k, n)$.
rows.license: arXiv-derived (studies-role extraction; per-paper license at REC time)
rows.class_notes: Named conjecture that r-stable Kneser hypergraphs have the same chromatic number ⌈(n−r(k−1))/(r−1)⌉ as the full Kneser hypergraph; candidates (Reed list-analogue, hypergraph minor colouring, matchings) do not match, so promote under hypergraph-theory.
